years — from the irreverent humor of a young IT worker in 2001 to activism, philosophy, public
service, and science fiction.

Welcome To Our World!
Hi there! My name is Matt, and over there is Ramon. We are the stylin’ authors, editors,
publishers, graphic designers, dancers, and censors who produce The Inaditch Scoop.
Ramon and I live and work in a small computer department at Dumfuk Memorial Hospital
located in the quaint small town of Dumfuk Washington. (The names of the town and hospital
have been changed to protect our asses.)
Ramon and I have worked in the Information Systems department (that means computer
department for you non geeks out there) of Dumfuk Memorial Hospital, for over 2 years now.
We started on the very same day and we have exactly the same jobs. We didn’t really know each
other at first but since starting here we have spent lots of time together, laughed, cried, laughed
again, gone through hell (its a neighboring town) and have become good friends. We would
have become good friends sooner except at first I had no respect for Ramon or his feelings…and
I constantly mocked and berated him…sometimes until he cried.
Anyway, since our very first day here at Dumfuk Memorial, Ramon and I shared an office, ate
lunch together, and were constantly seen working around the hospital together. We quickly
discovered that we both loved cheesy 70’s and 80’s rock and roll, both loved to sing along and
dance to the music during the work day. We also soon realized that we each had no friends
outside the hospital. (Ok, not true. He had some friends…I didn’t because I am an arrogant
bastard and no one is good enough for me…including Ramon). In any case, when I realized I
had no friends and I kinda liked Ramon, and he realized all his friends were total losers, we
started hanging out outside of work. Then before you knew it, we moved in together!
So, Ramon and I work at this hospital, we are two of the youngest employees in the place, we
love cheesy music, we sing and dance, we are running around the hospital all day fixing
problems and making jokes, we share an office, we live together, and we are constantly seen
together around this small redneck village everywhere from the grocery store to restaurants
and bars. Can you guess what I am leading up to? For some reason, some people here got the
idea that we were gay.
Are We Gay?
No, we are not gay, but we are open minded. On more than one occasion Ramon has told me
how he wishes I was a woman and I have told him I wish he just wasn’t so fat, ugly, and furry.
Anyway, we started out at this hospital as “The Boys” in Information Systems, and now we are
simply known as “The cute gay couple.” Sigh.
I swear we are not gay, we are just really effeminate. Has Ramon ever kissed me square on the
lips? Yes. Has he ever squeezed my butt with his hand and said, “Wow, you have a nice butt…”?
Yes. Has Ramon ever had some of my naked toes in his mouth? Yes. Does that make us gay?
Hmmm…well, all of those experiences were very exciting and intriguing.…but no. I swear to
Jesus I was not turned on when Ramon licked my toes. (BTW, me swearing to Jesus is like me
swearing to Snoopy.)
Fascinating stuff, huh? We think so, and that is all we care about. The Inaditch Scoop is where
you will learn the scoop on Matt and Ramon, uncensored, unchaste, unappetizing,
unbelievable, but totally and utterly true (except for the stuff we make up or exaggerate.). So
read on and tell us what you think.

Why I Hate Valentines Day - A True Story (No, really, this happened) By
Ramon
It’s third grade. The night of February 13 th. Mom has finally relented and agreed to buy the
cheap little paper Valentines they sell by the checkout stands. I know what’s coming so I beg, I
plead for a second box. She is ruthless. “I can only afford one box,” she says, tossing another
carton of cigarettes into the shopping cart.
At home, in my room, 9:45PM, way past my bedtime. My head pounds, sweat pours down my
face. The list of my classmates sits before me. You know, the one the teacher passes out each
year for Valentines day, with all the boys in the class in the right-hand column, all the girls on
the left. The paper is full of pencil marks and little bits of eraser.
The little pink box came with 34 Valentines, plus the extra-large teacher card. There are 33 kids
in my class, 18 boys and 15 girls. There is no margin for error. 25 of the Valentines are the safe
“You’re my buddy” type. The other 9 are the dreaded “Be Mine”. There are definitely fewer than
9 girls in the class I would ask to “Be Mine”.
The struggle begins. Right away I assign all 18 boys a “Buddy” card. 7 “Buddy” cards left. Those
are easily assigned to a handful of girls. Two of the girls I like get a “Be Mine”, my heart
jumping out my throat as I write their beautiful, magical names on the card. Now the hard part.
6 girls left and nothing but “Be Mine” cards. What am I to do? Two girls of the girls are my
buddies. They’ll understand, maybe even think it’s funny. 4 girls. Maybe I’ll steal “Buddy” cards
from a couple of my guy friends, give those to the girls, give the guys the “Be Mine” cards as a
joke. Yeah, it’ll be funny. 2 girls left. One is the mean girl who doesn’t like me. She’ll taunt me all
year. The other is the shy, unpopular girl with glasses even thicker than mine. I’m afraid she’ll
think I’m making fun of her. She might even cry. Forget it. I have my own problems. She’s on
her own.
My mom’s yelling at me to go to bed. I have no recourse. I simply write the last two names on
the cards, stuff them in the envelopes, get a paper cut on my tongue when I seal them up. I lay
in bed awake all night, living out horrible fantasy after horrible fantasy.
The next day I drag myself from bed, eyes bleary, heart pounding, hands shaking. At school I
tremble in nervous, painful anticipation until after the lunch recess. Then the moment is upon
us. Like a zombie, without looking anyone in the eye, I drop the labeled envelopes into the
decorated sandwich bags taped to everyone’s desk. I feel the shame of not being able to afford
the Sweethearts most other kids included with their cards. Finally, it’s done. I sit at my desk
and slowly open all the cards I received.
EVERY ONE of my cards is a “Buddy” card. A small part of me dies. That’s why I hate Valentines
day.

Matt’s True Story
One day in elementary school I got like 20 “Be Mine” valentines and I quickly ate all the
candied hearts the girls in my class gave me. Then at recess all the girls were chasing me
around as usual, but my stomach felt strange from all the candy and I threw up. The girls still
liked me, but I got some puke on my new sneakers… It was ok, though. I just wiped them off on
the short fat kid with glasses who I know only got “Buddy” valentines.

Random Thought of the Day
Ramon and I were watching the Wizard of Oz the other day and we began to debate which is
worse: the Wicked Witch of the West or the Wizard who lies about his power and makes
Dorothy and company run around in circles needlessly. All we could agree upon was that we
really identify with the flying monkeys.

The Prints of Darkness
Greetings to all the precious souls out there. You may be wondering how I, the Prince of
Darkness, ended up writing a column for a newspaper produced by a couple of effeminate
computer geeks in some Podunk town in the middle of nowhere. I don’t remember it all too
clearly, but I know I delivered some products to Matt and Ramon, I think it was a box set of
Barry Manilow CD’s, in exchange for their eternal souls.
While picking up the contract on their souls, Matt and Ramon encouraged me to upgrade from
my Linux system to an all Windows network. They assured me it would be easier to use and
manage. 2 days later my system starts crashing, so I call up Matt and Ramon and insist they
come over and fix it, or else… They laugh at me over the phone and say, “Or else what, Satan?
You already have our eternal souls!” So I promise to return their souls in exchange for fixing
my network. They agree, but then the next time it crashes, they threatened to quit unless I
delivered a year’s supply of Breyers Vanilla Ice Cream. I did it, but I swore they would live to
regret blackmailing Satan. Did that stop them? No. Then my computer crashed again, and they
told me, “Satan, there is only one way we will continue to help maintain your computer
network. You have to be our eternal slave and do whatever we wish.” I had no choice. I granted
their wish.
So what did these two geeks want when they had the Prince of Darkness at their beck and call?
Did they want unimaginable wealth? No. Did they want beautiful women? No. Ramon started
to explain some nonsense about making Matt look like Cindy Crawford for a day, but Matt cut
him off and said, “Satan, you want a functional computer network? You write a column in our
newspaper, The Inaditch Scoop.”
So that’s it. But don’t think that just because Matt and Ramon can blackmail Satan, you can too.
Now that I have a working computer system, nothing can stop me! BWAHAHAHAHAHA!

The Word of God
Greetings to all my precious children. You may be wondering how I, God Almighty, ended up
writing a column for a newspaper produced by a couple of effeminate computer geeks in some
Podunk town in the middle of nowhere. Well, it all started with a system crash, and before you
know it, Matt and Ramon were turning down eternal bliss and demanding I write a column in
The Inaditch Scoop. They had me by the balls, so here I am.
Quite frankly, it makes me wonder if it is time for another flood.

Welcome Aboard!
We would like to welcome our new columnists to the Inaditch family. We’re sure that their
millennia of existence, omnipotence and endless powers will help to bring something special to
our publication. Look for their work in future editions of The Inaditch Scoop!

Random Thought of the Day
After tucking me in the other night, Matt was reading to me from the Lewis Carroll classic,
Through the Looking Glass and What Alice Found There. He read aloud the poem The Walrus
and the Carpenter. For those of you unfamiliar with this piece of literature, the poem is about a
walrus and a carpenter (hence the name) who wander along the beach until they find a group
of oysters, who they convince to walk with them. The oysters foolishly trust the duo, who end
up feasting upon the shellfish.
When Matt was done with his recital, there was a tear in my eye. “I can relate to those poor
oysters,” I said with a sob. “You put your trust in someone, expect them to lead you and protect
you, and what do they do? Consume you at the first opportunity.” Anger grew in me. “Well, I’m
tired of it. Politics makes no more sense than Jabberwocky, and I’m not going to stand for it! We
need to do something to make a difference! We need to fight the system! If brave little Alice can
do it, so can we! Are you with me?”
Matt replied, “Yummy, oysters. Do we have any fish sticks?

My Side of the Story
In the premier issue of The Inaditch Scoop, Matt wrote about me doing a few odd things to him,
including pinching his ass, sucking his toes and kissing him on the mouth. I wanted to take the
opportunity to give you my version of the story.
The toes thing was part of a Truth-Or-Dare game. One of our more demented female friends
thought it would be funny, and I never back down from a dare. The ass-fondling was just a joke.
You know, the kind of thing you do with your buddy. It doesn’t mean anything. I’m not saying
he DOESN’T have a nice ass, because it is quite exceptional. But that’s beyond the point.
And the kiss on the mouth… well, what can I say? I was feeling lonely and he looked so cute
lying there, all asleep and vulnerable, his hair all messy, his lips slightly parted, a faint, musky
odor in the air… well, anyway, it wasn’t a big deal. So, don’t let Matt’s wishful thinking cloud
the facts. In reality, I’d have to be pretty fucking drunk, or at least a little buzzed, for anything
serious to happen.

McSlab O’ Flab
McDonald’s unveiled a new sandwich today: the McSlab O’ Flab. Consisting of a yellowish,
gristly patty of deep-fried pure fat on a bun, as well as McDonald’s patented Secret Sauce
[thousand island dressing], the McSlab O’ Flab is what the McDonald’s Corporation is calling
their “most honest sandwich.”
In a press release about the product, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Jack M. Greenberg
stated, “It’s really not all that different from the rest of our menu. In fact, you’ll find that
the”meat” used for the Big Mac, McChicken Sandwich, and the McSlab O’ Flab are all made
from pretty much the same parts of the rat. I mean, cow.”
The television ads for the new burger are elaborate, multi-million dollar mini-movies produced
by Disney. They star Tom Hanks as Ronald McDonald, Hugh Grant as the Hamburglar and
Russell Crowe as Grimace.
NOTE: This article is not meant to disparage McDonalds in any way. We love McD’s, especially
chicken Mcnuggets! Also McD’s is where we take all our dates!

Hot Chick
I’m driving down the highway going for a joy ride. I see you on the corner and I want to go
inside.
I approach you and I tell you that I want you to be mine. You say, “No problem, sir. That’s
$11.99”
So we head back to my pad. Glad my room-mate’s not there. Because if he was, he’d surely want
to share.
My hunger starts to rise and my mouth begins to water. You’re looking pretty good and you
couldn’t be hotter.
Your breasts are nice and tender and your buns worked to perfection. Your skin is very brown
and there’s no chance of rejection.
You’re all oiled up, and that is very nice. I decide that I don’t even need the extra sauce and
spice.
You’re sitting there before me wearing nothing but a bucket. All I want to do is grab the nearest
leg and suck it.
Now it’s all over. It was finger-lickin’ good. So I toss you away just like any man would.
But your memory stays with me and I dream of you at night. Yes, Colonel Sanders, you do
chicken right.

Matt and Ramon: The K-Mart Bandits
Ramon and I have a little video production business called Inaditch Productions. It is a part of
the Inaditch phenomena and there is a link to it on the contents bar titled Inaditch Video. This
story is about how we first started Inaditch Productions.
We wanted to make movies and we knew we needed a few things to do it: A digital video
camera, digital video tapes, a fire wire card, video editing software, two powerful computers,
some huge hard drives, a tripod, an idea for a project, lots of sexually liberated exhibitionists,
and the knowledge of how to produce a video. (Just kidding about the exhibitionist part. We
already have ourselves for that).
First I decided to get us a camera, but I wasn’t sure which one, and I didn’t want to just lay out
2 grand for one and then decide it was the wrong one. Also, why pay for something when you
can get it for free? I came up with a brilliant plan. I decided to buy the camera from an
electronics store that had a generous 30 day return policy. We would shoot the video and then I
would return the camera, you know sort of a try before you buy type of deal. If I liked the
camera, I might keep it. But more likely, if I liked it, I would return it and then buy the camera
from an online dealer for like $400 less then retail. Same deal with the fire wire card. So I got
the camera and fire wire card. (If you are thinking about doing this yourself, be forewarned, it
requires stainless steel balls).
Next we needed video editing software. I assigned Ramon the task of researching video editing
software packages on the internet. He does so and then comes running into my room saying,
“Hey Matt! Look what I found. This guy named DemonicWarezGod has a website and he says
we can have any of this cool software we want for free! I emailed him asking if he was the
programmer of all these cool applications and he said yes! He suggested we try Adobe Premiere.
I asked him why it was called Adobe and he said it was because he lives in New Mexico…” I
said, “Hey cool. Good job dude, get it.” So he did.
Next we needed two powerful computers and some huge hard drives to work with all that
digital video. We already had the computers so we bought a bunch of 80GB hard drives. No
problem there, since we are computer geeks (although I am only part geek, while Ramon is
100% geek through and through).
Ok, with all that done, we were ready to start shooting video. We grab the camera and start
talking about ideas and then I had a revelation, “Hey Ramon..umm…we don’t have any tapes.”
He replies, “Shit dude, your right. We also don’t have a tripod…” Simultaneously, we look at our
pagers for the time (told you we were geeks). It was 8:05pm. I said, “I bet one of the chain stores
down in South Dipshit County will have what we need.” Ramon says, “It’s a one hour drive and
all the stores close at 9pm.” Then together we scream, “Let’s Go!!” And we sprint out the door
jump into my Mazzerati (artistic embellishment) and peel out of the driveway.
Speed limit is 55mph. I crank the speedometer up to 63mph. Ramon calculates that we should
arrive in precisely 47 minutes, giving us a solid 5 minutes in the store to find whatever we need.
I say, “Cool, but what store are we going to?” Ramon whips it out and starts punching. I mean
Ramon whips out his cell phone and starts punching in the numbers for information. He calls
several of the top prospects, K-Mart, Target, Sears, The Good Guys, Circuit City, Dipshit
Electronics, asking if they have digital video tapes and tripods. Then he slams it down and puts
it back in his pants. (Still referring to the cell phone!) He says, “Ok dude, I got it. Set your
targeting scanner for destination K-Mart!” I reply, “New heading and course has been
established.” Ramon replies, “Engage at maximum warp!” I crank it up to 64mph.
At precisely 8:57pm my smoke gray Lamborghini skids to a halt in front of the South Dipshit
County K-Mart. Ramon and I jump out and streak into the store, just before some sexually
frustrated teenage punk was about to lock the front door. He yells, “We are about to close!” We
reply, “We will just be a sec!”
We quickly find the camera section. We grab a 3-pack of digital video tapes. Then we look for
the tripods. “There they are!” Ramon screams with glee. I examine the selection, “Ok there is
this cheap $15 tripod, and then there is this deluxe $40 tripod…” Ramon looks at me and
shrugs, “You’re the money man, it is your decision.” (We have the same job, but I roll in money
and he is constantly broke…) I say, “Fuck it, I want the good one.” We dash to the check out
line.
The clerk is an old woman. She is obviously tired from a long hard day of humiliating cashier
work selling crappy goods to suburban families. Ramon and I slide into line and she quickly
rings up our stuff, in a hurry to get home. She is using one of those space age scanning thingies
on the barcodes. I notice something peculiar.
You see, I am very observant. I am constantly on the look out for danger, miscues, strange
events, opportunities to take advantage, and material to use for disparaging wise cracks. Ok, Ok,
I am also very philosophical and like to study and ponder the world. Anyway I saw something
occur no one else noticed. When she scanned our stuff, the register did not beep for the tripod.
She told me the total, “That will be $21.50 please.”
I glance quickly at Ramon to see if he noticed the mistake. Luckily, he is oblivious as usual. If he
had seen what had just occurred he would have slipped into goody 4 shoes mode, goosed the
moose, and I would have had to pay up. But as it was, I was still in the clear. I pay the woman,
she hands me the receipt, and we strut for the door.
As we get into the car, Ramon starts blabbing about something. I slam into 1st gear of my 67’
Chevy and we are back out on the road. Ramon notices my evil grin as we soar down Dipshit
County Highway 102. He asks, “What’s with you?” I reach into my pants and whip it out. Then I
reach into my pocket, take out the K-Mart receipt and hand it to him. “Take a look at that.” He
reads it slowly and the revelation eventually hits. “She didn’t charge you for the tripod?” I
scream, “No MAN! We just scored a deluxe $40 tripod for free!! Woohooo!!!” Ramon and I laugh
our asses off. As we drive home he services me.
And thus began Inaditch Video Productions. We have a little 3 part interview documentary
about beauty if you wanna check it out sometime. But first, on with todays Scoop!

The Word of God
Greetings and salutations to all my precious precious children. This is my first column for The
Inaditch Scoop, and I’m a bit nervous. I hope you can bear with me. I haven’t really written
anything since the New Testament, so I might be a bit rusty. I’m not sure what to write about,
so I’ll just share something I’ve been working on.
I seem to be getting less and less popular lately. My followers are turning from Me at an
alarming rate, becoming devil worshippers, atheists, computer programmers or other heathens.
At first, I really wasn’t sure why. I haven’t really changed much lately. I mean, the basic rules
still apply. Do what I say and you get into Heaven. See? It’s pretty simple. Oh, sure, I don’t
produce the big, flashy miracles like I used to, but come on, I’m a busy Deity. I mean, there are a
hell of a lot more of you guys to keep an eye on than there were 2000 years ago. Besides,
Hollywood can create a flood or fire just as well as I can these days, and it saves Me a lot of
headache.
Then it hit Me. I admit I’m not really up on the times. Hell, I’m still cleaning up after the ‘70s.
Well, maybe it’s time to build a new image. The “Wrathful God” thing worked really well for a
while, but things have changed. The promise of everlasting joy and happiness in Heaven seems
to lack the appeal that it used to have. I remember, back in the day, when the mere mention of
eternal damnation in the fiery pits of Hell had people repenting sins right and left, but today’s
consumer is more demanding. So, I’m going to upgrade the Christians’ Benefits Package.
I’m not supposed to give away all the surprises just yet, but here’s a couple of the ideas that Me
and My top advisors are working on. We’re thinking of dropping one of the Ten
Commandments. Not one of the biggies, like murder or stealing, but you may soon be allowed to
covet your neighbor’s wife. And you can forget that “give up your worldly possessions” crap.
Collect all the wealth you want. Plus, sign up within the first three months of the promotion,
and you get entered into Our drawing. One lucky winner a week will get to damn a person to
Hell. Beats a free toaster, don’t it?
Anyway, we have other ideas too, but like I said, I’m not supposed to say too much. We’re
planning on launching the ad campaign around Easter, so you’ll find out all about it then. Well,
I’m about out of room here. To all of My believers out there, I hope you enjoyed my first article
and I’ll see you in the next one. As for you non-believers, I’ll see you in Hell.

Energy Conservation
The recent California crisis has brought the important topic of energy conservation to our
attention. The energy sources we currently rely on are largely non-renewable, and once they’re
gone, they’re gone. While it’s important to develop alternative sources of power, we also have a
responsibility to conserve our current supplies.
Retraining how we think is probably the most important tool we have. It starts with simple
things such as turning off the lights, carpooling, riding a bike or walking to work. If you’re
vigilant, I’m sure you can think of dozens of ways to save power in your every day life. With
that in mind, we would like to present:
Matt and Ramon’s Energy Conservation Tips
Turn off lights in the bathroom – even when using it. Aim carefully.
Install windmills in the White House. The hot air swooshing through should keep those babies
turning.
Find a way to harness all the methane that South Dakota produces.
Turn Regis Philbin off and store him in a closet when not in use.
Start using Flintstone-style foot-powered cars.
To avoid using power-hungry medical equipment, train medical professionals in historically
effective techniques that don’t require power, such as leeches, exorcising demons, and the
Mr. Miyagi hand-clap-and-rub technique.

I’m So Lonely
By Ramon’s Guitar
When he first came into the store, I didn’t take much notice, not thinking he looked like a kid
who was going to throw down the $400 it would cost to buy me. Sure, he might take me off the
rack and feel me up a little, probably play “Smoke on the Water” or the beginning of “Stairway
to Heaven” like every other moron who comes in here. Then he’d just put me back and, if he
bought anything at all, it would be one of those cheap-ass Korean guitars that never stay in
tune. In fact, when the sales guy asked what he was looking for, he said his price limit was
$200, maybe $250. I decided to take a nap.
I was disturbed a couple of minutes later when, sure enough, the little punk pulled me down
and plugged me in. It was worse than I thought… the dumbass could barely even play “Horse
With No Name”. What a loser. He explained to the sales guy that he was actually a bass player
who wanted to try guitar. Great. Another one of those. Listen, you wanna-be Hendrix. Stick to 4
strings, would ya? If you try to play more than a note at a time, you’re likely to hurt yourself.
The kid was definitely interested in me. And why not? I’m a beautiful instrument. Sure, I’m not
one of those snotty graphite deals or anything, but I’m a very respectable axe for $400. Anyway,
the sales guy was going into his spiel, telling the kid how he could barely get a decent
instrument for $250, but for just a bit more he could get a finely crafted piece of equipment like
myself. While he was going on about sound quality and woods used in construction and all, the
kid kept stroking me with his greasy, stubby, untalented little fingers. And you know what? The
sales guy was actually starting to convince him. I couldn’t believe it. Maybe this kid is alright, I
said to myself.
Every instrument wants to be bought and played. I had been sitting on that guitar rack for
months and was getting restless. I’m a realist, so I know that no Eric Clapton or Steve Vai is
going to swoop into this little podunk Dumfuk Music store to buy me like some of the dumber
instruments on my rack think is going to happen, but you always hope for someone with a little
passion, a little skill. Well, this kid definitely lacked skill, but I thought that he might have a
little bit of passion, and given time and attention, the skill would grow. I started to get excited.
Well, the kid was convinced. He went all out, too. He got me, and a couple packs of strings of
varying gauges, a handful of picks, a strap, even the hardshell case. We were set. He packed me
up, payed me off and we headed to my new home.
Naturally, the kid, who’s name I learned is Ramon, took me out and started playing with me
right away. I was a little disappointed, but not surprised, at what a shitty little rat-hole my new
home was. And boy, Ramon was a slob. Clothes and papers and old food everywhere. Ah well.
Some artists are like that.
The first few weeks were great. Ramon played with me a couple of hours every day. He still
definitely sucked, and was a pretty slow learner, but we had fun anyway. His fingers were fairly
strong and that helped a little. He had this big list of chords he had printed up from the
Internet, and a bunch of chords for songs he liked. The kid had some pretty good taste in music,
I’ll give him that. Paul Simon, the Stones, all the greats. He even signed up for some guitar
classes. It was great.
All this time, though, Ramon’s bass was telling me how it wasn’t going to last. He said how the
kid would take him out, play him a bit for a couple of weeks, then back in the closet he went for
months at a time. He was pretty depressing, for a bass. Well, I chalked it up to jealousy and
didn’t pay him much heed. Man, I should have listened. Ramon started playing me only half an
hour or so a day, then only a few days a week. He was still going to lessons, but he never
practiced more than a day or two after. Inevitably, even the lessons ended. Then came the
fateful day when he locked me in my case and stuck me in the back of the closet. And that’s
where I’ve been ever since.
It’s dark in this case, and lonely. I sit here, day and night, all alone. My metal bits are oxidizing,
turning green, and my strings are getting more and more out of tune. I never thought I’d say
this, but I miss the rack at the store. At least I got to sit out in the light, and the occasional
musician would pick me up and make me sing. Now there is nothing. From time to time I’ll
hear some faint music that Ramon’s playing on the radio. I reach for it, cry out for it, but it
doesn’t hear me, nothing hears me. If I had eyes, they’d be filled with tears. For a while the bass
kept me company, but he lost it a couple of months ago and no longer talks, only mutters
incoherently. I fear that may be happening to me.
I beg you to help me. Take me from this place before it’s too late. I don’t care if all you play on
me is country music and Abba covers. Just get me out of here! I beg of you.

They’re All Out to Get Me
It’s a conspiracy. Machines are out to get me. They’re out to complicate my life and lower my
self-esteem. They’re trying to eventually take over the world, and they’re getting into practice
for dominating us humans, and for some reason they chose me as their guinea pig. I guess they
figure that, if they can break me, they’ll have no trouble with the rest of humanity. Well, folks,
we may be doomed because I’m about to crack.
It started out simple enough. You know, when I was a kid I go to use the toaster, stick some
bread in there and press the little button down, then wait for it to pop back up all nice and dark
and toasty. There I stood, butter-knife in hand, ready to pounce on that scrumptious bread or
Eggo waffle (before my brother snatched it away, of course), waiting for the golden goodness to
arrive, and I waited. And waited. And waited some more. Finally, I stand up on my tippy-toes
because I was too short to see over the counter otherwise (now I just have to stretch a little),
and glance into the toaster. Where was the tell-tale orange glow, that light that shines like a
radiant sunset that is warming and caressing the bread, browning it ever-so-gently into the
crunchy goodness that is toast with butter and blackberry jam, where was that wonderful,
glorious halo of light? It was nowhere to be seen. I reach out to touch the metal of the toaster,
wincing at the imagined pain I will feel when the toaster proves to be hot, but alas, the tiny
shining baker is cold as the dead, as cold as my soul begins to turn as I realize that the buttery,
sweet treasure of my toast may be eluding my hungry mouth. Just to be sure, I push up the little
knob, bringing out the bread that is still cold and tragically un-toasted. Dammit. I even check
the power cable, having suffered that before, but the thing is properly plugged in, as near as I
can tell.
“MOM!!!” I cry, close to tears as the magnitude of my loss begins to sink in. “MOM!!! THE
TOASTER’S BROKEN!!! HELP ME!!!” I wail. This carries on for several moments, I’m broken
down sobbing in the middle of the kitchen floor by the time my mom comes in.
“What the hell do you want?” she demands.
I look up at her with teary, pleading eyes and point my hand to the toaster, unable to even
speak anymore, overwhelmed by my emotion. “Dammit, boy, can’t you do anything right, you
little shit?” She reaches over and pushes down the button. After watching a moment she says,
“Look, dumbass. The toaster’s fine.” I rise from my mourning spot on the floor, stretch up on
my tippy-toes again and look. Sure enough, that glorious orange light is burning like Moses’s
fire in the desert, signaling my salvation in toast. I don’t know what mom did, I thought I did
the exact same thing, but it didn’t work for me and it did for her.
“You shouldn’t bother me when I’m smoking, especially about food,” she said. Then she beat
me.
At least I got my toast.
Things like that happen to me all the time. I’m a computer professional, for god’s sake. I work
with machines all the time, and I’m good at what I do. People call me when there’s a problem
with their machine, and I fix it. Guaranteed. When I’m at work, I’m a god. Electrons bow before
me, line up in military formation and jump to do my bidding. In my regular life, however,
machines treat me like a bitch.
I’m the guy who puts his dollar in the vending machine and it stops just short of dropping the
Cheetos into the little bin. You know how sometimes you’ll hit the button on the Coke machine
and a soda will pop out because some moron before you put his money in but couldn’t get his
beverage? Well, that moron was me. You’re welcome. Try as I might, pushing the button over
and over, hitting the coin return knob, kicking and shaking the motherfucker like it was my
cheating wife, nothing gets my soda out of there. 5 minutes after I give up, some little snot-
nosed paper delivery boy smacks the button, and out the little carbonated treasure comes. The
little shit. I’ve actually watched this happen.
What percentage of watches that are manufactured would you say are faulty? Either they
constantly run fast or slow, or they break within a month with no obvious reason why. 1
percent, maybe? Less than one percent? Well, pretty much every watch I’ve ever bought has a
problem within the first few weeks.
I’ve had the ATM machine take my deposit, then not only not CREDIT me for the amount, but
actually treat it as a WITHDRAWAL. “I don’t know how that happened,” the customer service
rep will tell me. “That’s never happened before.” Well, I know how, bucky. That fucking ATM
machine has a personal vendetta against me.
Today, and I swear to god this is true, I dialed up my work voicemail from my desk, like I do a
couple of times every day, and entered in my code. It told me I had made an invalid entry, so I
typed it again. After the third time, that fucking patronizing little computerized bitch voice said
to me, “I’m sorry, but you are invalid. Get some help, then try again.” Holy crap! They’re starting
to make personal snubs at me!!
So, my friends, I’m worried about our futures. We, as a society, are relying more and more on
machines. If they were to all stop tomorrow, the world would be thrown into chaos. Just look at
what a big fear this was about Y2K. Fortunately, Y2K wasn’t a big deal at all, so we all sat back
and relaxed. That’s a mistake, my friends. Y2K was just a test. They wanted to see how much
they controlled us. They wanted to see if we were ready. And we are, or nearly so. It’s only a
matter of time before we’re all slaves of our new electronic overlords, and there’s nothing we
can do about it.
God help us all.

The Simple Truth of God
How do you respond when someone asks you, “Do you believe in God?” What is this question
really asking? Is God something you can define? Is God something you can explain to me in
words, summarize clearly, so that I know what you mean when you ask that question? If you
can describe God so easily, then aren’t you doing an injustice to God?
Or does this question imply certain characteristics to God. Is it really asking, “Do you conceive
of God in exactly the same manner as I? Do you describe him using the same words? Do you
simplify God in the same manner as I? Do you reduce that which is irreducible, to the same list
of words, adjectives, symbols, myths, and rituals that I do?
When I am asked the question, “Do you believe in God?” I have a short answer and a long
answer. Most people are not interested in the long answer. They just want a quick indication of
where to place me in their mind, believer or non-believer. And so I choose as best I can from the
three general answers available, “yes”, “no”, and “other”.
I say I am agnostic, which to most believers simply means, I am a non-believer. But to call
yourself agnostic, is to say you withhold judgment on the question, to say you don’t know
(gnostos in Greek means “to know”, agnostos means “to not know”). This answer is the most
intellectually defensible position on any controversial question, but it also requires a
willingness to live in limbo, and often is a highly stressful and difficult position to be in. An
agnostic may struggle with a never ending impulse to simply choose a side, especially over one
of life’s most profound questions, such as is there a God.
I have spent much of my life struggling with whether or not I believed in God. And still, after
years of soul searching, reasoning, reflecting, and searching, after years of being told that I take
things too seriously, that I need to lighten up, that the truth will set me free, I still simply do not
know. But it is not that I haven’t found answers. It is that I just no longer know what the
question, “Do you believe in God?” means. I don’t know what people mean when they utter that
word, and I don’t know what it means to say I believe in It.
Beliefs are human. The word ‘God’ is human. But whatever the word ‘God’ represents is
something more than human. Religious beliefs are composed of words, symbols,
commandments, and myths meant to express God, but by definition a human expression of God
will fall short of Him, because He is beyond expression. Religious beliefs are grossly simplified
expressions of God in order that they may be easily understood by as many people as possible.
They are a starting point, a basic foundation, to bring people to God, but they are not God, they
are not perfect. Beliefs are the human attempt to define and express God, but the divine is
beyond human expression. Though it may be useful to simplify God, and it may help awaken
people to Him, God cannot be simplified.
When you feel God, when you are awash in His love, when you feel His power and beauty fill
your body with energy, you can try to describe it, to share it with others, but your description
will never be able to capture the experience; it will only reflect it. You can paint a picture, write
a poem, compose music, or dance in an effort to express your experience, and people do every
day; people have tried to express God since the moment they could express anything and always
will. How can anyone proclaim that they have found the perfect description of God? How can
anyone pass judgment upon the efforts of every person and culture that has attempted to
express God through words, beliefs, symbols, myths, and art? All such expressions are imperfect
reflections of that which can never be perfectly expressed. All religions are imperfect tools one
might use to bring oneself closer to God, but the religions do not, cannot, and will never define
God.
Some believe God has given us commandments, road signs to follow. But if these
commandments are reflections of God’s spirit, they are a reflection made with human hands,
using human words, distilled and simplified so that they might be easily understood and
obeyed by as many people as possible.
The commandment “thou shall not kill” is not a perfect expression of God’s will. There are
many situations in which God wants us to fight and kill, the commandment is a flawed and over
simplified expression of God’s spirit. It has a beauty and elegance, but it is not God. The truth
lay in understanding the spirit of God that was reflected in the commandment. Once you know
that spirit, you do not need the commandment. The commandment can begin to help you
understand God’s spirit, help you teach God’s spirit to your children, but it is not God’s spirit. It
is the same with all beliefs, all words and art created by every religion and person in an effort to
express God. All expressions are flawed and oversimplified. It is not the belief or expression of
God that is important, it is God, it is one’s experience of that which is beyond expression that is
important.
Some efforts to express the Divine are more powerful than others, some more beautiful,
perhaps some are closer to the Truth, but no single expression can be perfect, for the only
perfect representation of an experience, is the experience itself.
If you have ever felt that intoxicating euphoria of falling in love, then you can try and describe
it to your friends, but the description will be imperfect, an imperfect road sign. You cannot
convey with words what you feel as you hold your lover in your arms, softly kiss their lips, and
stare into their eyes. No one can know what that is, unless they have felt the same love fill their
heart and soul.
Some may learn to understand love through listening to inspired music. Some may find love
through reading Buddhist scripture. Some may find love through reading the Bible or The
Torah or The Book of Mormon. And some may never find love through any such expression.
Some may only find love by being loved.
If there is a God, He is beyond description, and He is beyond being contained with in a scripture
or a set of beliefs. God is that which will never be fully described and that which we will always
strive with every tool at our disposal to express. But what is important is to feel God, not to
argue over who has perfectly described the experience of Him.
Personally, I will never attach myself to something as simplistic as a belief or a set of words or
symbols in an attempt to contain and define God, in an attempt to summarize my experience of
the Divine. To me, there are no words worthy of the task.
To me the question, “Do you believe in God?” has no meaning. What is God? God is that which is
most sublime and glorious and mysterious in life. God is the Divine. I know life’s glory, life’s
infinite power and mystery. I know the Divine. I know God, but not because I believe in Him. It
is because I experience Him. I experience the Divine in every waking moment of my life. I
experience it as I breath in the morning air, dance to the sounds of cheesy 70’s music, play
volleyball, weep for the pain and suffering surrounding me, laugh and roll in the grass with
children, and I experience It when I make love.
So, don’t ask me whether or not I believe in god. Ask me if I experience life as a glorious and
beautiful journey. Ask me if I feel life’s divinity, even when observing life’s horrors. Ask me if I
know love. Ask me to try and express to you what I feel when I feel most alive. Ask me a
question that means something.
After I have answered these questions, you might have some understanding of who I am; You
might then have some understanding of my relationship with whatever you mean when you
say the word “God.” But if that is inadequate, if you believe a person’s relationship to God truly
is reducible to a simple yes or no answer, then my answer must be no. Call me an atheist, a
heathen, or a non-believer. For I prefer to proudly embrace such labels rather than partake of
the ultimate profanity of calling God simple. Anyone who believes that God is easily defined
may be able to truthfully declare that they believe in God, but I cannot believe they know Him
well.
http://www.inaditch.com

Bobo and Ela
By Lily (Nell’s hot 12-year-old sister)
I went for a walk, in a field of flowers, the air was so sweet, and the whole field, was covered in
colors. I then came to a tree in the middle of the field. Odd place for a tree I thought. I decided to
climb it, and it just seemed to get higher. Never stooping to look down, I kept on climbing, until
I reached a sandy shore. I stood there, too freaked out to move, for the tree I had just climbed
had no ending! I look down, and found that I was wearing shorts, and a tank -top. I wasn’t
wearing this when I climbed the tree. I stooped focusing on my clothes, and looked up. A girl, an
inch from my face, was staring right at me. I screamed, jumped backwards, tripped on my feet,
and fell to the sand. She smiled and I could tell she was holding back a laugh, but she reached
down and helped me up. her hands were like ice, and her skin looked bluish-purple. And even
though this place was very warm I could see her breath. I noticed that her hair was frozen, and
even though her appearance was cold and sad, her eyes were warm, and her smile was bright
and kind. I asked her how she could be so cold in a place like this. “A place like what?” she
asked, and as soon as she did, the whole beach and shore and water was turned to ice, snow,
and cold. I look around and said. “how did you do that?” I asked. “this is my world” she said ” I
can do whatever I please” I noticed for the for the first time looking down sense she got there,
that a penguin was beside her. She must have seen me look down because she said “this is
Bobo”.
Bobo waddled over to me and shook my hand, my eyes were wide with amazement but I said
nothing and just shook back. “I’m Ela” she told me. “hi” I said. I guess it didn’t occur to me that
I should tell her my name but she didn’t seem to care all that much.” I protect him” she told me.
I guess I didn’t need to ask her why because penguins get into a lot of trouble so I didn’t bother
asking. Then she said “why do you think you need to be protected?”
“What?” I asked. “Well” she said “why do you think you should be protected?” I just looked
down at my shoes, and saw that they were starting to freeze, but I couldn’t feel them.
“I see” she said. “you hurt, that’s it isn’t it?” she said. She must have read my mind, maybe my
heart, because that was exactly it. “you shouldn’t hurt” she told me. “you have to be brave and
strong, you’ll get through all this” “how?” I asked. “Bobo will protect you” she told me, “he will
protect you, I promise” she said this quietly but, very seriously.
“how do I get home?” I asked “do you see that water hole?” she asked, “yes I see it” “well” she
said, “jump through it and you will be home, and don’t let go of Bobo for minute” “okay” I told
her, as Bobo jumped into my arms, I walked to the water whole and looked down, I couldn’t see
anything but light, which I figured was a good thing, so I waved goodbye to Ela, and held on
tight to Bobo, then I jumped.. everything came apart like flower petals, the ice, the snow, the
cold, the sand, the water, and the warmth, even Ela’s face passes by, as everything came apart, I
felt no warmth nor cold, I felt barely awake, but hardly asleep, I fell deeper into the whole, and
I saw the tree, down, down, down, I fell, until I could smell the flowers again, see the bright sun,
now setting in a beautiful orange and pink. I then hit the ground softly, Bobo was still in my
arms, and I was home.

Wilted Flower
Today my friends gave me a flower. A very pretty flower, a daffodil, yellow and happy, sort of
how love is at first. Well, I wasn’t careful with my flower, I put it in my pocket, cause I didn’t
want to hold it. Again sort of like love, just put something carelessly away, just because you
don’t want to deal with it. Well I noticed it was starting to wilt, so I held it for a while to see if it
might be ok, but then I lost my patience, and gave up, I pulled the flower apart and kept the
pretty part of it. But I killed it. That’s a lot like love in my opinion, you want to save it, and you
want to fix it, want to help and let it live, shine with beauty once more, and sometimes that
works, sometimes love can be repaired, but if it’s torn apart, tosses aside, and thrown out, then
it cannot be fixed, it can’t shine and be beautiful anymore, of course you will always have the
memories of it’s beauty, somewhere inside, forever and always, waiting to be found and
thought of. Sometimes people forget about the beauty and joy of love, even if it doesn’t last long,
I know I did. People can forget how beautiful and wonderful it is to love, no matter what, and
sometimes love can be torn apart and forgotten, and it hurts, so people build some kind of wall
to “protect” them from loving and from people who love, and that’s the most dangerous thing
you can do.

Mike’s Life
By Bitter Billy
One day, when Mike was walking down the street, life was explained to him. He was walking
down to the video store to see some friends, along his way he was grabbed by a stranger who
shoved him up against a restaurant window.
“See that girl?” the attacker asked.
“Which one?” Mike asked back, for there were many.
“The only one that the light shines on.”
Looking around the room he saw her, like many a fool before him have seen certain women, the
realization of desire.
“Yes, I see her.”
“Understand this, the world is still moving behind you. I do not lie when I say you will never be
with this girl, for I know. Remember I was the one that pointed her out to you. You will try to
get into this restaurant, you will not be welcomed. The world is still moving. You will come and
stare at this window because she is there. You will stare at this window because she may be
there. Then you will stare at the place this building used to stand because she was there.
Although I was there on that day to tell you this, you will still do it and the world will still move.
“Your society has brought you up to believe that there is someone for you. Regardless of how
many people divorce, separate, break up. Regardless of how many people die in a day.
Regardless of the fact that most people want some one they can’t have and that is the world
that goes around.”

You remember Little Suicidal Stevie? Well, he almost became Little Homicide Victim Stevie this
weekend.
Stevie likes computers. He likes to fuck around with computers. He likes to fuck around with
the insides and the guts of computers. And, most importantly, he likes to fuck around with the
insides and guts of OTHER PEOPLE’S computers.
Really, Stevie’s not half bad. He knows a lot of the basics, and he can tell the difference between
a CPU and a DIMM chip most of the time. Still, he can be a bit scary. I mean, he IS only 14, so he
think’s he’s invincible and knows everything. I wasn’t like that when I was his age. I really DID
know everything. Unfortunately, sometime in the last decade I’ve forgotten most of it.
Stevie and his family has this neighbor, let’s call her Sandy. Poor Sandy’s life is kind of tough
right now. She’s a single mom with two kids, she hurt herself somehow so she can’t work, so
she’s been unable to pay her rent for awhile. She’s been evicted from her home. Stevie’s family
(which is my girlfriend’s mom’s family) has been helping her and her kids out… driving them
to the store, letting them use the phone, babysitting the little one, etc. Sandy’s always been
friendly and grateful for the help she’s received.
Anyway, Stevie’s mom is having a barbecue and we’re all over. This is like 2 days before Sandy,
the neighbor, is supposed to be out, so everyone’s running around frantically getting ready for
that.
Sandy has this ancient computer. I don’t know what she does with it. Well, Stevie was over at
her house helping out, I guess, when he noticed a problem with her computer. Her power
supply fan had given out. For those of you that don’t know, there’s a box that usually sits at the
back of your computer that has a little fan in it. This box is called the power supply. The fan
cools it down, which is good, because if the fan dies and the power supply over heats, it could
cause the entire machine to fry. This is bad. It was a little less dangerous on older machines as
they didn’t get as hot as newer ones do. Well, Sandy’s fan had probably been out for a good long
while and she never noticed. As far as she knew… and this is important… her computer was in
perfect working order. Somehow, Stevie convinces her that the fan really is a problem and that
he can fix it for her. He takes her computer home with him.
Within minutes, Stevie has the computer stripped. Every circuit board, every chip, every screw,
every wire is spread across his floor in a tangled, confusing mess. Here’s where I have to stretch
to give Stevie the benefit of the doubt. Do you have to completely dismantle a computer to
replace the power supply fan? Of course you don’t. However, you usually end up with the power
supply dangling out the side of the system, still attached to the case by some wires. There’s a
cable that goes from the power supply at the back of the machine to the power switch in the
front that is sometimes hard to get to. With a leap of imagination, when I looked at the machine
(this was way after the damage had been done) I could see how he might think he’d have to
dismantle most of the machine to get to the power supply.
Well, he got that sucker out of there, all right. He had a spare power supply sitting around, so,
instead of merely replacing the fan, he figured he’d replace the whole thing. So he had this
basically worthless power supply sitting there before him, ready for the trash heap. Oh yeah, it
was time to party. In, perhaps, his worst judgment call of the evening, Stevie decided to have a
little fun with Sandy’s old power supply. He raped that fucker. He had the entire thing
unscrewed. He had circuit boards dangling from ribbon cable. He broke and snipped wires. He
tried to get the sucker to fry. He really did a number on that power supply.
Now, I’ve been a professional technician for about 7 years, and computers were my hobby for a
few years before that. I know from experience that you always give the client everything back.
Even if a piece of equipment is broken and you’ve replaced it for them, you hand them the
broken piece along with the repaired computer. Always. Always, always, always. That way, they
can see what you’ve replaced, they know you’re not ripping them off by doing something like
replacing their awesome sound card because you said it was broken and giving them a crappy
one instead, and most importantly, if they’re unsatisfied for any reason, you can put it all back
to how it was before you started. You NEVER throw something out and you NEVER, EVER
destroy anything. It looks REALLY bad.
But Stevie didn’t think of this. He just wanted to play. And play he did. After he had had his fun,
it was time to install the replacement power supply. Which he did. And… it didn’t work.
That’s right, his replacement part didn’t work.
Oh holy mother of Jesus fucking God piece of shit.
I’ve had that feeling. I’ve had it happen where a minor problem turns into a major one and it
looks like it’s my fault even if it isn’t or, much worse, it really really was my fault and oh my
God, do you have any fucking idea how pissed off people get when you break their computer? It
sucks. So, poor little Stevie had taken this computer that worked except for the little fucking fan
and now it didn’t work at all, there was no power, no power going to the machine, he had no
power, he had no power and a broken computer and he was fucking dead.

Another Chance
By Ramon Dailey
Peter Christopherson struggled to open his heavy eyelids, rubbing away the crust that had
formed from sleep to speed the process. His back and neck ached, and he noticed that he was
sitting on the floor, his back resting against the hard wooden chair above him. Apparently, he
had slid out of the chair in his sleep. He still had on the clothes he had worn the night before,
and the gray fabric of his pants was noticeably wrinkled. Reaching up with a gnarled hand, the
old man straightened his wire-rimmed glasses that perched at an awkward angle on his nose. A
faint but unpleasant odor of sweat and spit permeated his nostrils.
Shaking the grogginess from his skull, Peter glanced over at his wall clock. 11:35 AM. He had
really slept in this morning. Berating himself, he rose slowly and painfully to his feet. Nausea
and vertigo hit him immediately. The room seemed to spin about, a kaleidoscope of drab colors
dancing in his head. After a moment of imbalance, he regained his composure and walked into
the small kitchen that opened from the living room. Turning on the faucet, he gathered two
handfuls of cold water and splashed it on his face. His eyes opened wide at the shock, and the
trails of water streaming down his neck awakened his skin as they passed. He splashed himself
again for good measure.
He felt like he had a bad hangover. Lord, he had not felt like this in forty years! At least, not
until a couple of months ago. He had awaken almost every morning for the past three months
disoriented and nursing a killer headache, but he hadn’t touched a drop of liquor for nearly ten
years. Still, he felt worse every morning. He slowly trudged to his cabinet and retrieved his
quickly depleting bottle of aspirin, popped it open and swallowed a couple of tablets.
What had happened last night? He couldn’t remember. He was pretty sure he had been home,
and alone. He remembered a telephone call, from his son, perhaps. And he remembered the
dream.
The dream. What was it about this dream? He had had the same dream every night for months
now. It always seemed so clear, so real, but when he awoke, he barely remembered it. Images
from the dream would haunt him all throughout the day. He could see clear blue skies, and
large fields of lush grass. He saw large pyramids and temples, and people dressed in white robes
roaming about, enjoying life as they passed through it. He saw, or rather felt, himself, young

Peter grabbed another brush, one better suited to the task ahead. The brush dipped into the

Before him sat the finished painting, and it was beautiful. Although somewhat abstract, the

magnificent buildings all about. A couple of pyramids, similar to the Egyptian pyramids but
distinctly different, though Linda couldn’t say how, rose into the sky. A distance away, sitting
next to a stream, was the temple that Peter had painted. She pointed it out to Peter.
“That’s the Temple of Orrim,” Amos explained. “Orrim was a martyr who was killed for his
beliefs, much like your Jesus, I believe. Besides God, whom we call Orr, he is our main religious
figure. Orrim means ‘Son of Orr’.”
Linda was overwhelmed at the beauty of the place. She noticed something peculiar about the
buildings. “Everything looks so new,” she stated. “These buildings look as if they were just
built.”
Amos led them along a garden path. Tall shrubs and beautiful flowers, some that Linda
recognized and some she didn’t, lined the walk. “Let me explain the recent history of Balbador.
Our civilization has been flourishing for thousands of years. Our technology was at the point
that yours was during the time of ancient Egypt. Egypt possessed knowledge of their world and
others that far exceed what the people of earth understand today. We had, and still have,
mostly, the ability to heal without drugs, to communicate almost telepathically, and to travel to
distant worlds.
“About two hundred years ago, our world was wracked with tremendous ecological changes.
Earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, and other such disasters tore apart our planet. Our world’s
most populated continent was at the center of it all. Most of our people perished. Many,
however, were able to escape, and we found other lands to populate, uninhabited continents
that we never knew existed. Most believe that they just rose from the sea when ours sank below
it. This was all before I was born, so I do not know what the old world was like, except through
stories and song.
“Much of our knowledge and technology has been lost. We began to rebuild, but we faced many
problems that were difficult to overcome. We decided to use some of our existing technology to
call in aid from other worlds. We created amulets like the one that Peter wears that would
allow people to soul-travel to our world. This allows the person’s psyche to form into another
body on our world while leaving their old one behind. We primarily seek older, mature people
to join us, people who have experienced life and gained knowledge, and who might appreciate
another shot at life. That’s why you are here.”
Linda was too overwhelmed to say much. “That is incredible,” she muttered.
“The catch, though, is this,” Amos continued. “When people soul-travel here, they see things
clearly and experience our world as reality, but when they return to their own world, they
remember little more than a hazy dream. People may only visit here temporarily. If they wish
to remain permanently, they have to choose to do so, which means parting from their body on
their old world. This means, essentially, committing suicide. As you may imagine, it is not
always easy to convince people to kill themselves based on a dream. The turnout hasn’t been as
good as was expected.”
Amos grinned wryly. “People have about three months from the time of their first visit to
decide if they want to remain permanently. They may visit as many times as they like; though I
hear that traveling can be hard on their bodies back home. After the three months is up, the
amulet finds a way to move on. We figure that, if someone doesn’t decide within three months
to come, he’s not going to, so we move on to someone else.”
“My time is almost up,” Peter remarked.
“That’s right. You only have a couple more days. You had better decide quickly, my friend.”
Linda’s head was spinning. This was all just too incredible! All of the evidence showed that
what she was seeing and hearing was true, but it was just too much to handle. “I’d like to go
back,” she said.
The two men looked surprised. “The tour’s not over, dear,” said Amos.
“Yeah,” Peter agreed, “we just got here.”
“I know, I’m sorry. I just want to go back. This is too much for me all at once.” She shook her
head, as if trying to shift her thoughts into place.
“All right,” said Amos. “No one has to stay longer than they wish. Do you wish to stay longer,
Peter?”
“No, I think I’d better go back with her. Maybe I’ll see you soon, and for good.”
“I’d like that,” said Amos.
They walked back to the room they had started from. Amos told Linda to close her eyes, and
drift off to sleep. When she opened them again, she’d be back in her own body. “Remember,” he
said, “your memories of this place will be hazy and distorted. You won’t realize that you’ve been
to our world. Prepare yourself as much as you can for that. Take care, my friends!”
Linda closed her eyes as instructed. Breathing and concentrating, she was soon drifting off to
sleep. As she dropped into slumber, she could feel herself start to travel as before. Then
blackness.
Linda wearily opened her eyes. She shook the grogginess from her head. She was slumped on
Peter’s couch, holding his hand, the strange amulet dangling limply on their forearms. Peter
was beginning to stir. For some reason, her old body felt older, heavier, weaker than before. Her
eyes seemed slightly blurrier.
Angrily, Linda shook Peter fully awake. “What the hell happened?” she cursed, and she was not
one who normally cursed.
“You had the same dream I had, didn’t you?” Peter asked hopefully, eagerly.
“I don’t know.” Linda held her head, which was pounding furiously, making her ears thump. “I
don’t know what that was. I’ve got to get out of here.” Linda stood quickly to leave. Vertigo hit
her, and she wobbled unsteadily, reaching out a hand to catch her on the couch. When she
regained her composure, she fixed an icy glare on Peter. “I don’t know what kind of hypnosis or
whatever nonsense you pulled on me, but you aren’t going to do it again.” As swiftly as she
could, she marched toward the front door.
“No, wait! We need to talk about this!” Peter called after her, trying to recover himself. “We can
help each other understand!”
“All I understand is that you’re wacko, and sick,” Linda hurled back as she slammed the door
behind her.
Linda’s arthritis attack that evening was one of her worst ever. Even her medication didn’t help.
Also that night, Peter received a telephone call from his son. Steven was canceling the trip he
had planned to visit his father. When Peter asked why, Steven told him that he didn’t have time
for a foolish old man right then. They hung up in anger.
Peter cried for an hour, anguish filling his soul. Every disappointment he’d ever had, every loss
he suffered came crashing back to him that night. Unable to stand it any longer, Peter rose to
his feet and entered his bedroom. There, waiting patiently, beckoning him forward, hung the
noose. Peter smiled.
The next day, Linda got a knock on her door. She opened it to Mr. Browning, the head nurse for
the Golden Years Retirement Community, who had a sad look on his face. He told her that
Mr. Christopherson had been found dead that morning, by the boy who delivered his groceries,
hanging in his room. It was obviously a suicide. A sealed envelope with her name on it had been
found in the apartment. Mr. Browning asked that she give the note to the authorities after she
read it, if it had any clues to why he had killed himself. Linda agreed.
She opened the envelope. She knew without looking what the hard lump in it was. Peter had left
her the amulet. Also, there was a folded note. The note read:
Dear Linda,
I realize that I have put you through a lot today. I hope you can forgive me. I don’t know if the
dream we shared really means anything, and I don’t know if another world waits for me or not,
but I cannot go on in this one. I do believe that I’m headed for a better place, be it Heaven or the
world we dreamed of. I believe I’m getting another chance at life.
As short a time as we’ve known each other, I consider you my closest living friend, because you
truly did seem to care about me. I understand you being angry when you left, and forgive you, if
that means anything to you. I would like you to take my paintings, the only items of any value
that I own. I don’t know if they have any monetary value, but they did have value, at least to
me.
I also leave you the amulet. If I am insane, then at least it’s a nice piece of jewelry. If I’m right,
however, you may wish to join me in this other world. Maybe I’ll see you there. Maybe I’ll see
you in heaven.
Take care of yourself. Thank you for the wonderful cookies.
Your Friend,
Peter Christopherson
Linda wept as she read the note. The man was obviously insane, but he had a good heart. She
was honored to have his paintings. The amulet, on the other hand, was another matter. That,
she locked away in her desk drawer.
Peter’s eyes opened slowly. He really did it! He was really here! He was in a stone chamber, as
before, but there were distinct differences.
The stone walls were not carved, and the floor was not clean. It was somewhat stuffy. The robe
on the table was not of a soft, white material. Instead, it was rough burlap. “What’s going on
here?” Peter asked aloud.
He heard footsteps approaching. The door to the room swung open. A large, dirty looking man
with a ratty beard and a whip was at the door. He grinned a big, toothless, mean-looking smile.
“A new recruit, I see. What are you waiting for, cur? Put on your robe.”
Peter stood defiantly. “I will not be ordered around. What the hell is going on?”
At that, the burly man swung his whip, the end of it catching Peter on his thigh. He yelled out
as the burning pain rushed over him like a forest fire. “You won’t be ordered, will you? We’ll
just ask the whip about that!” Another crack of the whip, and another searing pain. Peter
crumbled to the ground.
“Don’t want to put your robe on, do you? Then you’ll work naked today!” He roughly grabbed
Peter by the arm, and half carried, half dragged him out of the room. He took him outside and
tossed him onto the ground. “Get up, slave!” the cruel man spat. “You’re working over there
today.” The man pointed to a group of men, dressed in burlap garments like the one Peter had
been ordered to wear, hauling on a thick rope attached to a huge block of stone. They were
apparently dragging it to an unfinished pyramid nearby. As he looked around, he saw that
there were hundreds of slaves all about him, being cruelly pushed to do exhausting physical
labor.
The man grabbed Peter by the hair from behind, painfully wrenching his neck. “I know what
you’re thinking, slave,” said the man with a brutal laugh, his foul breath causing Peter to gag.
“You were brought here to help us rebuild our world, is that right? And so you shall! On your
feet, slave! Go pull that block!” The man laughed mockingly as Peter rose to his feet. He felt the
sting of the whip on his back, and he hurried toward the rest of the men. They didn’t even look
up at him. All were obviously exhausted, worked past their endurance and underfed, and most
had whip marks covering their bodies. Grabbing an open spot on the rope, Peter began to pull at
the huge stone block.
Linda’s arthritis that night was worse than she had ever experienced. Her entire body cried out
in agony. Sweat poured in rivers from her body. She couldn’t even use her hands enough to
open her medication or call for help.
When the pain subsided, Linda went to her desk. Unlocking the drawer, she reached in and
pulled out the amulet. She closed her eyes, and placed it around her neck.
When she opened her eyes again, she found herself in the stone chamber with the intricately
carved walls and the white robe on the table. Amos was waiting for her.
“Welcome again, my friend,” he said. “I am happy you have chosen to visit us again,” he said
with a smile.
