Basic General Assembly Agenda
2011/11
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
General Assembly:
The general assembly is an opportunity for everyone to gather and discuss important matters
that impact the movement. It is also a decision making body that operates utilizing a consensus
process. Outlined below is the order in which the NYC general assembly is generally held.
Opening (10 MIN):
  •    Introduce the Facilitation Team (Ask for Consensus on Team)
  •    Review Hand Signals
  •    Review Step Up, Step Back
Agenda – Items that require a group consensus to decide on or break-out groups to generate
new ideas and potential fixes. Agenda items might be proposals, break-out groups, initiatives or
speakers.
Proposals – Items requiring the consensus of the GA. These are well thought out, written down
or typed out, proposals that require group feedback and approval. It is encouraged that
proposals are worked out in a working group or have the support of a large group before being
brought before the GA.
Order of Presenting a Proposal
  •    The proposer reads the proposal, twice if necessary.
  •    The floor is open to clarifying questions or concerns, speakers should get on stack. The
       proposer can answer questions or address concerns directly as they come.
  •    The floor is then open to ‘friendly amendments’. These are amendments to the current
       proposal, not a new proposal or question/concern. It is up to the proposer to accept or
       decline friendly amendments.
  •    Once everything has been discussed and friendly amendments have been address the
       facilitation team will move for consensus by asking for a temperature check.
  •    If the check is a mix of agree and disagree, that is not a meaningful consensus and the
       item will probably need to be tabled, set aside until the next GA, and refined. If it is
       about 70/30 in agreement with the proposal and the proposer isn’t interested in tabling
       the item, the facilitator can move for a 9/10 vote.
  •    If there is consensus, everyone seems to agree, the facilitator must asks for ‘blocks’.
       Anyone presenting a block will need to explain why and if the block is not rescinded or
       the proposal is not removed the facilitator will move for a 9/10 vote.
  •    We DO NOT want to vote, that means some people are excluded or ignored. But if the
       issue is critical we will do a straw poll, raising of hands in agreement, and if the
       facilitation team sees 9/10 agreement the proposal passes.
To contest an old proposal that has already been passes, draft a new proposal that would
remove or invalidate the old one.
Working Group Report Backs (15-20 MIN) – Report backs for already formed working groups to
inform everyone of events, actions or meeting times.
Announcements (15-20 MIN) – General announcements about events, initiatives, etc. Not a
chance to soap-box or push an agenda, that comes at the end of the GA.
Close GA – Makes sure everyone knows the GA is closing with a rally cry or cheer. Let everyone
know the people’s soap-box is next and that they can stay or go if they like and the soap-box
will not be facilitated.
People’s Soap-Box/Open Forum – A chance for anyone who wants to talk at length to do so and
have their opinions heard.

Basic General Assembly Agenda v3
2011/11
──────────────────────────────────────────────────


A Simple General Assembly Outline from a different source: http://piratenpad.de/axsIOgdO63
Schematic, practical example of an Assembly Agenda 1) Welcome and Positive
Presentation : Assembly is effective celebration of the power of the people. 2) Summary of the
consensuses reached in the previous Assembly and all outstanding issues. 3) Roles of each
of the team members. 4) Explanation of the concept “Assembly”: We do not “vote”, we reach
consensus. 5) Explanation of the concept “Consensus” (direct/indirect). Explanation
of consensus building process. 6) Reminder of the gestures used in an Assembly and
suggestions of how to express oneself verbally 7) Reading the Agenda out loud. 8) Sub-
Working Groups without specific proposals for the Assembly, only information which does not
require consensus. 9) Sub-Working Groups with specific proposals for the Assembly.
Opinion > Debate > Resolution or Adjournment 10) Individuals with specific proposals for the
Assembly.                     Opinion > Debate > Resolution or Adjournment 11) IMPORTANT
NOTICES/ANY OTHER BUSINESS.
  •       Citations, general interest information, latest news, etc.
  •       During this round, there is no opportunity for debate. , rather taken up by the pertinent
          working group or commission.
  •       Important: if it is necessary to cut short this round because of lack of time or tiredness,
          announce this and tell those who have not had a chance to intervene in this round that
          the subjects they wanted to mention will have priority in the any-other-business round
          in the next Assembly with encouragement to also be put online.
12) Conclusions and notification of time and place of next Assembly. 13) Closure and
acknowledgements, including a message of motivation and reminder of common
purpose (memorable words : verse, a piece of good news, quotation or a short text, etc.)

Facilitation Guide
2011/11
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
If you are the meeting facilitator, you have a critical role in making the meeting a positive
productive experience for all attendees. The facilitator role ensures that meetings lead to
action. Talk is cheap. Action is what changes things.
First: Read this if you have not yet. This covers the basics of facilitation.
  •       Consensus Basics - http://www.nycga.net/groups/facilitation/docs/consensus-basics
  •       Brilliant Cheat Sheet for Facilitators of small or large groups
Things For a Facilitator to Remember
  •       Before the Meeting (or at the beginning of the meeting)
  •       Clearly define the purpose of the meeting - If the meeting does not have a clear purpose,
          then it is appropriate to “crowd storm” at the meeting to see where the group needs to
          take the discussion.
  •       Keep the purpose statement vague and general. The details can be discussed. It is very
          good to write the purpose on a white board or piece of paper as a visual reminder – or
          anchor for the group.
  •       Be Patient. Do not rush. - Consensus is a powerful thing- but you must be very careful
          not to rush it. The moment you impatiently push a discussion forward – potentially
          ignoring someone need to say something – you risk losing that person. The power of
          consensus is you move forward as a whole. It is not about everyone getting their way-
          but it is about everyone having their say!
  •       Temp Check – You build consensus to act from the ground up – just like building a
          house. You start at the foundation – defining the purpose of the meeting – and work
          your way up from that. A Temperature check is a quick test to see if the piece you just
          put in place is solid enough to move on. Use it frequently.
  •       Create an Agenda/ Plan for the meeting – If you don’t have any agenda, it is easy to hold
          a meeting that accomplishes nothing- and leads to no action. An agenda doesn’t need to
          be complicated. Here is a very high level basic agenda all meeting should follow:
  •       Set the Tone for Meeting Process
  •    Ask for permission to facilitate – temp check.
  •    Review meeting process – hand signals, stack, etc
  •    Ask for a minute taker – preferably on a laptop and a stack taker. (I have found if you
       have more than 6 people in a meeting, I need a stack taker to be most effective)
  •    Define Purpose of the Meeting - Temperature check if everyone agrees on the purpose.
       If not, crowdstorm it.
  •    Define time limit of the meeting - temperature check that everyone agrees this is how
       much time we have today.
  •    Facilitate – Facilitate the meeting step by step towards actions to achieve it’s purpose.
  •    This is the meat and bones of the meeting. You may or may not have a detailed agenda
       of topics for this section. If you don’t have any details for this section – then crowd
       storm it with the group.
  •    Watch the Clock! – Fatigue is the enemy of consensus. You set the time limit at the start,
       stick to it unless you have a 90% consensus to extend it. Before everyone passes out
       from meeting fatigue you need a consensus on the next step-
  •    When and where will the team meet again.
  •    Review any tasks that were taken on during the meeting.
  •    Make sure minutes are given to a person who can post them on the website.
  •    Congratulate the team on their hard work.
  •    Stay Calm – Meeting attendees will get fired up and emotional at times. It is critical that
       the facilitator keep a cool head at all times so you can continuously watch for the best
       ways to guide the discussion.
  •    Don’t Get Down On Yourself - Facilitation takes practice. The first few times you do it,
       you will probably not do it perfectly. That’s ok. Dont’ beat yourself up. Learn from the
       experience. Debrief with other facilitators about what happened and what you might
       have done more effectively.
Facilitation of Meeting Disruptions
Ambrose Desmond – OWS
Here is a suggested process for facilitating meeting disruptions.
Overview:
  •    Create community agreements.
  •    If someone goes off process, use straw poll to ask the group whether they want to hear
       them or continue with previous business.
  •     If they want to hear them, let them speak and use straw poll to test whether their
        concern is shared by group.
  •     If the concern is shared, use straw poll to see if group wants to discuss this concern or
        more back to its previous business.
  •     If someone continues to disrupt after a clear consensus that the group doesn’t want to
        give them time, use a straw poll to see whether the group considers this a disruption,
        reminding them people can be asked to leave fo repeated disruptions.
In detail:
  •     At the beginning of the meeting:
  •     Create a list of community agreements through brainstorming. Staying on process will
        always come up.
  •     Ask permission to check in with the whole group if someone starts going off process by
        saying, “If someone goes off process, I’ll check in with you to see if you want to continue
        with the process or hear them. If you decide to hear them, I’ll check in to see if their
        concern is shared and whether you want to discuss it. Is that OK?”
  •     When someone starts going off process
  •     Do not try to use your authority as facilitator to get them to stop.
  •     Acknowledge they want to speak by saying, “I hear you really want to speak right now.
        Let me check in with the group to see if that’s OK.”
  •     Do a straw poll by saying. “Here are two options. Option one is we let this person speak.
        Option two is we continue with the process we were having. How many are for option
        one? How many for option two?”
  •     If less than 10% of groups want to hear the person say, “It seems like the groups wants
        to continue with their process right now. Someone from facilitation support can
        hopefully help you find a time to speak.” Have a support person come talk with them
        about a more appropriate venue.
  •     If more than 10% of groups want to hear them, let them speak. Listen actively and try to
        ascertain their concern or what they want the group to do differently. Once you
        understand their concern or suggestion, use straw poll to ask the group how many
        people share this concern.
  •     If less than 10% shares the concern say, “It looks like there is not a lot of support for this
        concern.” Then temp check going back to previous business.
  •     If there is more than 10% say, “It looks like there is some support for this concern.” Use
        a straw poll to determine if the group wants to shift the meeting to discussing the
        concern. There will be some shared concerns that don’t need to be discussed.
  •   If someone continues to disrupt after a clear consensus that the group doesn’t want to
      give them time, use a straw poll to see whether the group considers this a disruption,
      reminding them people can be asked to leave fo repeated disruptions.

Intro to Process (10mins)
Welcome
  •    “Welcome to the Port Townsend General Assembly! Thank you for your participation!”
  •    Confirm all can hear the speaker. If not, teach group human microphone.
  •    The meeting time for future General Assemblies, working groups, meeting minutes, and
       everything else will be found on occupyporttownsend.org
  •    Reminder of purpose of General Assembly
  •    The purpose of a General Assembly is to help us find our common ground so we can
       work together to solve problems and improve our world. A General Assembly is open to
       all people.
  •    A General Assembly is a Consensus Based Group. Consensus Decision making means:
  •    We are not here to debate and win arguments. We are here to collaborate.
  •    The aim of Consensus Building is to build upon our common ground.
  •    All participants are asked to actively listen, rather than merely be preoccupied with
       preparing our response.
  •    all opinions need to be considered when generating consensus, making it difficult to
       assimilate and apply, thus it may require a long process….all that’s needed is time.
The process and methods used to facilitate this general assembly are designed to make the most
directly democratic, horizontal, participatory space possible; each tool (hand signals, etc) is
about opening space . If you have suggestions for how to improve the process of facilitating,
please participate in the Process and Facilitation Working Group which is meeting Tuesday 5-
6:30pm at the Undertown in the back room.

FAQ
2012/03
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
What is the Occupy Movement? The Occupy Movement is a leaderless International Protest
Movement with an “overriding commitment” to Participatory democracy. What is a protest? A
protest is an expression of objection, by words or by actions performed to create pressure for
change. What is a social movement? A social movement is a type of group action organized
around a single issue or set of issues, or around a set of shared concerns. What is Occupy Port
Townsend? Occupy Port Townsend is a leaderless and nebulous group of people who come
together and organize action in solidarity with many of the prevalent themes of the
international Occupy Movement. These themes include:
  •    Using an organizational structure of Leaderlessness, Participatory Democracy,
       Consensus, and Egalitarianism
  •    Focusing on political and social issues that current participants feel most strongly about
       which include social and economic inequality, government corruption by the influence
       of wealth and corporate power, education, healthcare, war, environmental issues, and
       more.
What’s the point of trying to fight corporate power? There is nothing you can do. One of the
most common attitudes encountered by Occupy protestors is ironically not hostility towards
our fight against corporate control of government, but rather it is a cynical acceptance that
“this is how the world is and there is nothing you or I can do about it.” Why do you do direct
action? Why don’t you all just vote? Many of the participants in Occupy do vote and use other
“acceptable” tactics to push for change. Voting and traditional “main stream” and “normal”
tactics can sometimes effect change and if you feel comfortable using them, go ahead. The
purpose of direct action including non violent civil disobedience is to create pressure upon a
system when all the acceptable forms of pushing for change are inadequate. The fact that the
system accepts and allows a tactic, like letter writing, is to some extent because the tactic
doesn’t stress the system out very much. If you want big change, you need some way to build
some significant stress on the system. Why are you trying to stop Jeff Co, all institutions,
businesses, and individuals from using the big banks: Bank of America, Chase, Wells Fargo, and
US Bank? The USA is not a democracy. It is not a government of the people, by the people, for
the people. The US political system is controlled by money. This is not equality. This is not the
vision of democracy. We want this to change. This is a very hard problem to wrestle with.
How do you use a broken system to change that same system?
One formula we have adopted: To weaken the power of wealth, we will do everything possible
to weaken the power of the wealthy. The big corporations, lead by the big banks, are the most
powerful holders of wealth. If we all stop using them, we weaken them. This is the greatest
action we can take to undermine their power. So stop using them. We invite you to stop using
them. We demand that all public institutions stop using them. We invite you to help us
encourage all businesses to stop using them. If enough local communities rise up and come
together around that simple concept, stop feeding the corporations, then we can create a
climate where we can finally fix this system. Why don’t you all get a job? Strangely, one of the
most common things heard yelled at Occupy Protestors seems to be “Go get a job!”. Many
Occupy supporters have jobs. In fact, many of us feel we are risking our jobs and much more by
participating in Occupy protests – but we feel it is worth it. There are more important things
than our own individual jobs, money, and comforts. A better world is possible if we all come
together to make it a reality. Why not join us?

General Assembly Dec 3
2011/11
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
The Occupy Wall Street movement is alive and well, and taking root in our rural setting.
Occupy Port Townsend began at a pre-Occupy rally in October, when Jeanne Simmons, Port
Townsend resident and mother of two, invited people to gather every Saturday from 12 to 2 next
to the Farmerís Market at Lawrence and Taylor. The movement has been growing, at the
Saturday demonstrations, and in weekly meetings at coffee shops. Now, the public is invited to
the first Occupy Port Townsend General Assembly, on Saturday, December 3, from 3 to 5 pm at
Quimper Unitarian Universalist Church, on San Juan at 22nd Street.
The General Assembly will start making short-term and long-term plans for Occupy Port
Townsend actions. A kind of poetry of democracy, it is a direct, continual flow of
communication. Hand signals give constant feedback to speakers: ìagreeî, ìdisagreeî, ìi want to
speakî, or ìwind it up, pleaseî. A rotating group of neutral facilitators explain the meeting
process and guide the discussion to help the assembly build consensus. Stack-keepers keep
track of who wants to say something, and call first on those who speak least.
ìMany Americans are struggling with devastating circumstances,î says Simmons. “People are
losing their jobs, their pensions, their healthcare. Middle-class Americans are slipping into
bankruptcy, foreclosure, and homelessness. The latest statistics reveal that 1 in 3 children in
America lives in poverty. I think the number of people living with serious grievances reached a
critical mass this fall, and folks started taking to the streets and joining the Occupy Movement.”
Although there is no one spokesperson for Occupy, key concerns are being expressed daily, in
Occupy camps around the world, and through social networks like FaceBook and Twitter.
Occupy Movement supporter and participant O’Neill Louchard says, ìEach of us has our own
major concerns. Mine is the increased militarization of the police nationwide and the growing
prevalence of brutal tactics they use on peaceful persons exercising their rights to free speech
and assembly.î
A common grievance among Occupy participants is that corporate dollars play too great a role
in government.
“Corporate and Wall Street bank money have thoroughly corrupted our political process,” says
PT resident Doug Milholland. “Our democracy is hanging by a thread. The richest 1% of
society has stopped paying its way. The jobs that were going to trickle down went overseas
instead. Increasingly the 99% are losing jobs, benefits, pensions, and programs weíve paid taxes
for all our lives. The sense of crisis brings us together. We can sort out our differences later. Itís
only together, as individuals and groups, that we can turn this around,î says Milholland.
ìYoung students and graduates, looking at a future of joblessness and debts, started the Occupy
Movement,î says Doug Milholland. ìNow Occupy has grown into a big enough tent that people
of all ages, libertarians, progressives, union supporters, people who opposed the TARPS,
environmentalists, members of the Judaeo/Christian/Islamic faiths that emphasize social and
economic justice, and faiths like Buddhism and Society of Friends that emphasize peace, all find
a legitimate place there.
The goals of the Occupy Port Townsend Movement thus far have been to strengthen our local
democracy and economy, to stand in solidarity with the global Occupy Movement, and to
support other small communities in forming their own Occupy movements. Occupy Port
Townsend organizers hope that Port Townsend residents representing many causes, and with
diverse concerns, will attend the General Assembly. Our goal is to find our common ground and
work together to make real change.
For more information about Occupy Port Townsend, please visit
http://occupyporttownsend.org/, email occupyporttownsend@gmail.com, or
find us on Facebook.

Listen Look Find
May 16, 2012
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
What do you seek? In one word. What do you seek. Focus your being upon that one thing as
best you can. Then be still.
Do nothing unless your inner child, the watcher, the spirit that is the obverver, the will to
action within you gently pushes you toward that action.
Do not breath, do not move your eyes, listen for a nudge. Let the spirit of being have your body
and mind. Allow it to possess your body. Feel as it gently shifts your posture and breath. It will
awaken like a ghost given a body after ages of waiting.
When there is music- let the watcher dance. Let it move you as it will.
Do not do things because they “should” help you on your journey. Do not sit and meditate
because that is the thing to do. Sit so as to listen to the inner observer, the child, the spirit- and
do whatever it moves to do. Sit, until it nudges for movement. Stand, walk, breath, let the inner
child explore the world. If the child is lost, be still until it is found again.
Will a dip in icy water refresh your spirit? Perhaps. Listen to the child. Wait. Does it crave the
dip, does it move you to swim? If so, then dip. If not, then wait. Dabble. Move on. There is no
prescriptive path to life. An act in one moment may be perfect- yet is not perfect the next.
Listen. Just listen. Listen to being. Learn to explore with the pure authentic curiosity, learning,
and joy of the child spirit within. VN:F [1.9.22_1171]

The Observer. The Tao.
May 16, 2012
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
The observer, the actor, the inner child…. no words seem to label it. So I thought, perhaps just
describe it.
It is childlike- yet it is infinitely wise. It is patient and full of love. It is playful, curious, and
joyful. It is lively and energetic. It is eternal. It is infinite. And then as I appreciated the
strangeness of my wording…it reminded me of something else I have read. The Tao that can be
trodden is not the enduring and unchanging Tao. The name that can be named is not the
enduring and unchanging name.
The observer, the inner child, the infinite playful wise center of life within us is the Tao.

Mindfulness in Daily Life is Not a Question of Sustained
Monumental Effort
August 3, 2012
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
A realization that has emerged and really crystalized for me lately.
When it comes to mindfulness, seeing and following my dharmic path, it is not about sustaining
a continuous and perfect level of self discipline and conscious will power. I don’t have to
sustain mindfulness at the exact same level of vibrancy and richness. The thought that I was
failing in some way whenever my level of awareness lowered was making me feel defeated and
frustrated. Perhaps if I lived every day in a mountain meditation retreat, I could live
continuously with a sustained level of astoundingly vibrant mindfulness. But at this time in
my life, with my current rich and diverse life activities, a lifestyle I am open to evolving – but
not just destroying in the name of mindfulness – it seems my mindfulness, my conscious
awareness will often fluctuate along a spectrum. And as I said, trying to fight this, resist this
every waking moment is too much. The question that arose then, was if holding at a high level
of mindfulness every waking moment of the day is too much, what is the right amount? What
is the right level of effort? Right Effort Right effort has emerged as a critical concept for me to
come back to, especially if I start to feel particularly non mindful, nervous, confused, impatient,
frustrated. Instead of dwelling on frustration or just giving in to mindlessness or submitting to
whatever impulses are working on me, I think “right effort”. I don’t have to climb mount
Everest. I don’t have to conquer every force or situation that washes over me. But by thinking
of Right Effort, it reminds me that there is a choice between summiting every mountain and
just giving up. There is a middle ground – even if I know I am not going to utterly win a
particular struggle, it doesn’t mean the right level of effort is none.
Effort is Right Effort
So when I am getting swamped by a wave of emotion or experience that I know is going to
swamp me for a while – for I know I am not going to summon the energy and will at this
moment to hold perfectly steady and calm through this wave – I began experimenting with
putting some resistance in. Instead of giving in to the experience comepletely, I put some effort
into being mindful and aware through it – I began looking for a middle ground – a level of right
effort. I quickly became aware of a rather amazing revelation. It doesn’t matter how much
effort I put it- what matters is that I exert some effort to be mindful through the experience.
Suppose I am sitting in an environment that is very stressful – and I have good and valid
reasons not to just get up leave. Maybe I am at a social gathering, or at work, or watching a
movie with friends, and for whatever reason I consider important to stay in the environment
regardless of the stress that is being generated. The stress is building like a wave and I also
know I am not going to start meditating upon it at this moment. It is happening too fast, too
strongly, and the situation is such that I am going to get swamped by it. I may already be
upside down in my mental kayak and swallowing water. Instead of just surrendering to this
experience and waiting until it is over so I can go find somewhere to sit quietly and meditate – I
put some effort into regaining my balance and peace. And it seems, if we measured this effort
on a scale from 0 to 10, it is better for me to exert something sustainable and doable during the
experience, whether it is 3, 2, 1 or .0001, rather than just putting out 0 effort and waiting til
later. .001 is still infinitely more than 0.
Mindful effort seems to work like water or an ion space engine. How many moments are there
between now and the next 10 minutes? The answer is infinity. So whether you exert an effort
of 1, 4, 6, or .001, multiply that by infinity and what do you get? You get infinity. The only way
to fail is to exert 0 effort. That is the only way to guarantee 0. It is like a small drip of water on
a rock. One drip does little. A billion drips transforms the rock. Or think of an ion space
engine. It exerts a minuscule amount of thrust over an extremely long period of time resulting
in faster speeds than any other technology available.
So I actually think Yoda may be wrong on this one. There is a try. What is important is try.
Make an effort. The right effort is some effort. Only you can judge whether you are honestly
putting in an effort or being lazy and telling yourself you are making an effort. VN:F
[1.9.22_1171]

Why Seek Happiness?
August 8, 2012
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
I often embrace the metaphor of the tree when discussing the purpose of life and the pursuit of
happiness. A tree knows nothing else, but to doggedly seek to grow and flourish. It does not
complain. It does not wallow in resentment if it is planted in poor soil or some spot destined for
an early demise. It lives and it seeks to flourish with all its ability – until it is no more.
Likewise, a healthy human, accepts the reality of their situation, and shall work to flourish. To
flourish is to grow and explore, feel and learn, create and share, laugh and celebrate.
And yet, that logic, that reasoning doesn’t inspire me to reach for the stars. It does inspire me
and every step I take of growth and learning, creating and sharing, often leads to amazing joy
and expansion. And yes, I know if I continue to push the boundaries I will likely feel more joy
and awakening – which will feel amazing…but this simply doesn’t spark me to inspired right
effort.
I felt motivated. I felt determined. I felt happy. I did not feel an angst. Life is a beautiful
glorious journey and I was going to embrace it – still I felt something unclear within me. I am
seeking the flourishing growth of the tree, I am seeking happiness, but why really? Why did
that path, which I knew in my mind was the most noble and perfect path, why should I feel
that is so hard. Shouldn’t the joy and awakening be feeding and motivating me to seek more joy
and awakening. I am feeling rewarded with every healthy effort – but feeling rewarded is
strangely unsatisfying. I felt this incongruity of reward failing to lead to motivation and I sat
with this.
Some might call this “discomfort” I felt in my mind as “cognitive dissonance”. Or maybe you
might call it an “inner conflict”. One of the amazing things about meditation and the practice of
mindfulness, you don’t have to call it anything. I simply need to pay attention. I will sit and
pay attention and I will feel this “discomfort” in my being. I may not feel it clearly, I may only
feel the edges of it. It is like feeling my way through a soup and suddenly I touch upon
something sharp. And because I am sitting and paying attention, I am able to gently turn my
attention towards the “sharpness” and try to see it more clearly.
If I was not sitting still, if I was engaged in some sort of even minimal activity like Yoga, I may
not be still enough to feel the sharpness and immediately look at it. It is amazing how even the
tiniest of action, like stretching or even just shifting your position, can serve as a disturbance
that shakes up the ocean of our consciousness making everything in our being slippery like
swimming fish. Yet, if we are still, these things can become revealed and become like rocks
uncovered by a sinking tide, allowing me to touch them and feel their crevices, and examine
what they sit upon.
This mental discomfort, this confusion over my motivation was like one of these rocks. Why do
I seek happiness? It is not that I wanted to have a snappy elegant answer to this question. I
wanted to feel the answer. It is not about having the perfect words to describe the perfect
answer. It is about feeling a true fundamental motivation. Again, I could not have said this is
what I was seeking. I simply felt I needed this. I looked inside my being and felt a lacking, I felt
the lacking of a solid foundation to stand upon or a truly burning energy source to spur me to
reach ever further and deeper.
Then with this “lacking” feeling awakened within me, I happened across this quote: “All the
suffering in the world comes from wanting happiness for oneself. All the happiness in the world
comes from wanting happiness for others.” (Buddhist master Shantideva) Now you will likely
say to yourself, this quote is not that terribly unique. Many forms of it have been said in many
ways by many people. I think as I become more mindful and awake, I am noticing that we are
surrounded by all the answers we could ever seek. Every person, book, article, song, and
website holds countless answers to questions, if I am just able to ask and listen. It is not so
much about finding the right book or person, it is about reaching within myself to feel the most
urgent question at that moment. If I do that, almost anywhere I look for the answer will
provide some guidance, some learning. A well targeted question itself helps filter out the
irrelevant stuff, and helps one hone in on meaty and useful information.
So this quote hit upon something critical for me. “All the suffering in the world comes from
wanting happiness for oneself. All the happiness in the world comes from wanting happiness
for others.” This made me look at why do I seek happiness? For, is that the problem? Should I
not be seeking my happiness at all, but rather the happiness of others? Some of you might say
yes, but I clearly see pure selflessness as horribly flawed.
There is a dinner table story of heaven and hell that I was told when I was Catholic. At this
dinner table all the people had straight long arms and could not bring food to their own
mouths. This was the exact same situation in heaven and hell. In hell, all the people sat around
the table, which was full of luscious and tasty food, and they reached for the food and wept and
starved for they could not eat. In heaven, people sat around this plentiful table and ate and
were joyful, for they used their extremely long arms to feed each other. Thus, we are taught, be
selfless.
Yet, this story and the ideal of selfless action is deeply flawed. For we do not sit around a table
with arms only capable of helping others. We sit in a life in which we have arms that can help
ourselves and help others. More importantly, there is food and nourishment for our soul which
no one else can feed us. There is critical nourishment that only I can grasp and consume. If I
sit and wait for someone else to deposit in my mouth joy, meaning, understanding, inspiration,
peace, calm – I shall be left hellishly starved. We are blessed with legs, arms, eyes, and mind
and with these things we can find and feed ourselves the most gloriously valuable and
nourishing wisdom of life – and if we don’t do it, we shall never have it. Even more absurd, is
the idea some people have that they already possess these things and try constantly to shove
their answers down your throat.
One popular answer others will try to shove down your throat, “Don’t seek your own happiness.
Seek happiness for others.” And with this they tell you to spend your life only thinking about
what you can do to make others happy. Indeed, isn’t this what the quote above seems to say?
“All the suffering in the world comes from wanting happiness for oneself. All the happiness in
the world comes from wanting happiness for others.” Maybe you think it does. Maybe you do
not see the difference. This is why words are such a flawed conveyor of wisdom. It is not about
the words, it is deeply understanding the wisdom behind the words.
We sit not at a dinner table with deformedly long arms only capable of nourishing others. We
stand in a soup of life and our greatest and most direct power lay in what we can do to and for
ourselves. We also have the power to touch others, but this is not our greatest power.
Take for example healthy habits. Do you eat right? Do you exercise? Do you watch too much
tv? Do you smoke? Do you indulge in too much alcohol or drugs? Do you suffer from any
addictions, big or small? If you do, who has the power to help you? Who has the power help
you behave in a healthier manner? Other people cannot reach inside you and give you self
discipline. They cannot reach inside you and make you do healthier things. They cannot make
you see why you should want to choose differently. You have that power. Only you have that
ability to help yourself be healthy. If you do not do this, no one else can or will do it for you.
Suppose you did sit around a dinner table with excessively long arms. Everyone insisted, “Do
not think of yourself, rather think of others. Feed others!” And so everyone began offering food
to each other. Suppose some of the food was unhealthy or even rotten or poisonous. Do you eat
whatever is shoved in your face? Do you say, “No?” Or are you being too selfish if you think
about yourself in this manner? If you do not pay attention to yourself and what you are eating,
who else will do so for you? Do you expect to just trust that other people are watching out for
your well being?
You need to be selfish. You need to nurture yourself. You need to pay attention to your own
needs. You need to love yourself. Yet, as I looked at this statement, “All the suffering in the
world comes from wanting happiness for oneself. All the happiness in the world comes from
wanting happiness for others.” I felt something sharp, something important. I awakened to the
realization, I feel the greatest happiness when I share happiness. I feel the greatest inspiration
to seek, grow, learn, and explore when I know I am seeking to share all that I see, feel, learn and
discover. The thought that I am trailblazing up a mountain- only so that I might see more and
more glorious views – such a thought I find deflating. I don’t yearn to see further and further.
I yearn to see further and further and then help others do the same. It is not happiness I seek,
it is to share in happiness. It is not wisdom I seek, it is to share in wisdom. It is not learning I
seek, it is to share in learning.
These thoughts gave rise to a stream of memories, some of the most amazing moments of joy in
my life, and all of them, every last one of them had a critical amazing ingredient, other people.
The most astounding moments of laughter filled glorious joy always were connected to a
sharing of that joy in some way with others. Even my painting, which I spend tens of hours
alone creating, I see my joy in that art is deeply connected to the knowledge that other people
will see it – it doesn’t matter who or when – but others will and some of them may touch the
same spark of inspiration that made me make it. Even when I dance and sing alone in my
home, I am often thinking about how I am filling myself with happiness and I cannot wait to
share this happiness with others.
VN:F [1.9.22_1171]

Knowing What To Do vs Knowing Why You Do It
August 9, 2012
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
I find for most things, it is essential to know why rather than what.
I find I only succeed as far as the why takes me. Following a what without an adequate why is
like blindly following directions. It can lead to learning and perhaps will awaken you to some
reasons why.
But ultimately, know what is like holding a piece of fruit in your hand. It will rot and whither.
Knowing why, is to hold a glowing glorious magic compass, and you can simply follow it where

neighbors and your community?
Who has power over you and your life?
Who has power over the lives of your friends and family?
Who has power over your neighbors and community?
There is an old cliche saying, “Absolute power corrupts absolutely.” This saying is not actually
true. It misses the mark a bit. There is a big difference between how power effects a person,
depending upon whether that power is over themselves or over others.
Consider filling in the following table:
Who cares the most about you? Who has power of your and your life? Who cares about your
friends and family? Who has power over the lives of your friends and family? Who cares about
your neighbors and your community? Who has power over the lives of your neighbors and
community?
The answer to who cares about X the most is always X.
The answer to who has power over the lives of X is always X, Y, Z, K, J, P, M, etc etc…
Who is in position to make the best decisions for the health and well being of X is always X.
Anytime the person, entity, or group is not X and the person, entity, or group is making
decisions that effect the health and well being of X, the decision will likely be sub optimal, bad,
horrible, exploitative, or worse.
What if a small town in the USA, mindfully studied all the people, entities, and groups that
wielded power over their lives – and systematically acted to strip the power from any people,
entities, and groups who were not them. What would that look like? How far could this go?
How might they transform their lives for the better if they embraced greater power over their
lives? VN:F [1.9.22_1171]

misteps you can, but don’t dwell. It is of limited value. Focus on what is real. Focus on the here
and now. Where are you touching the wall? Can you smell the fresh air up above? Do you have
a firm grip or are you about to slip off and fall at this moment? What good is it to know how
you fell in the past if thinking about it prevents you from seeing your about to slip right now!?

experience every few minutes. It’s not just like a roller coaster where you go down a ridiculous
incline and scream “Holy Shit!!!!” and then you go through a loop de loop and again yell “Holy
Shit!!!!” and then you do it again and again. The difference being, every time you ride that

Meditation and Activism
August 19, 2012
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
Meditation is a label for an activity. Activism is a label for an activity.
The fundamental purpose of meditation is to help transform, evolve, grow yourself into the
most beautiful, happy, flourishing being you can possibly be.
The purpose of activism is to help transform, evolve, grow the world into the most beautiful,
happy, flourishing world it can possibly be.
Meditation comes with no rules or boundaries over what is acceptable. Meditation nurtures
mindfulness which brings clarity. You see where you are and you see where you wish to step
next. Whatever action is right, you take it.
Activism comes with no rules or boundaries over what is acceptable. If meditation is a tool to
help oneself take “right effort” to effect the health of ones own life, activism is the taking of
“right effort” to effect the health of the larger community, society, the world.
It is interesting that the word “meditation” seems to focus upon the step before action. Yet,
meditation is invariably connected to and essentially bound to the actions that an individual
takes in their life as a result of it. On the other hand, “activism” doesn’t really contain the step
before action, the step where an individual is evaluating what is wrong and what needs to
happen. Rather, activism really is just the label for whatever actions one does to try to effect
the desired change.
If “meditation” is the label for sitting, seeing, evaluating, weighing in order to know what to do
in an individual life. What is the analogous word for what groups of people do before they take
group action? A word that labels “group meditation” that is equally as powerful, pure, sincere,
and mindful as individual meditation?
Reflecting -> Sharing, hearing Weighing, Evaluating -> Studying, Reporting, Debating Thinking
-> Discussing Meditation -> Becoming Still -> Becoming present -> Seeing -> Feeling -> Waiting
->
Meditation as it relates to action involves becoming still, becoming present and mindful, seeing
clearly, feeling clearly, and waiting until action emerges clearly. Do we have many words that
describe groups of people doing these things together? I wonder what would happen if groups
of people made all 6 steps of meditation a group activity? Meditation groups certainly exist, yet
in my experience they stop short of discussing actions that impact the world – except for
actions that focus upon promoting meditation. What if groups of people regularly came
together to meditate and engage in activism together? What would that look like? What would
they do?

Egalitarian Economics
August 22, 2012
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
We all participate in the world economy. You probably buy things. Maybe you work for a
business. Maybe you own a business or a share in a business. Maybe you sell things. Why do
you do each of these things?
Why do you buy things? You buy things because you want them or need them. Fair enough.
Hopefully you are buying things because they help you live a healthy thriving happy life.
Hopefully you aren’t buying things to feed addictions or numb yourself from feeling how happy
you are. That’s a different topic. In an egalitarian economy, people will still buy things they
want or need.
Why do you start a business or work for a business? You start a business or work for a business
to…what? Why do you do this? Are their multiple reasons or is there truly only one reason?
This is a very big and very important question. This is worth thinking about deeply.
If you say, I work to make money (or I run a business to make money) then how much money
do you need to make?
If the answer is “I want to make as much money as I can possibly make” then why is this the
answer? Why do you need so much money?
“I need money so I can buy things.”
Sure, but why do you need an endlessly large amount of money to buy things?
“I am not sure what I want. I want to be able to buy whatever I want.”
Why do you want to be able to buy whatever you want?
“Because buying things is fun. It makes me happy to be able to buy whatever I want.”
I doubt that. Earn money in order to make sure you are able to acquire what you need to
survive and live a happy healthy life. What is a happy healthy life? Well now that is a really
good question. You don’t need money to answer it, you just need some time. As Thoreau wrote
long ago, The necessaries of life for man in this climate may, accurately enough, be distributed
under the several heads of Food, Shelter, Clothing, and Fuel; for not till we have secured these
are we prepared to entertain the true problems of life with freedom and a prospect of success.
In an egalitarian economy, the workers and the business owners do not engage in business to
make money because money equals happiness or the ability to buy happiness. It’s not about
money. Let go of money. You acquire money for only one purpose in a happy life, to make sure
you don’t die of exposure. Life is not about figuring out how to make more and more money.
The true problem of life is finding true happiness – and if money can’t buy you love, it certainly
can’t buy you happiness!
Therefore, the true purpose of business and economics for you, for a healthy human, is not
money. Don’t engage in business for the sole purpose of making as much money as possible.
Engage in business to make enough money so you don’t starve or freeze to death and….what?
What else could business and working be about if not making infinite money?
Maybe we need to go back to why you might buy things. As I said, hopefully you are buying
things because they help you live a healthy thriving happy life. Great. Could this exact same
reason be a reason to engage in business? I work and start businesses in order to help myself
live a healthy thriving happy life? Maybe this reason could even be expanded to include
others. I work and engage in business to help other people live healthy thriving happy lives?
What is left to decide after that? Oh yea. Which people? Which people do you work and
engage in business for? You and your loved ones? Your neighbors? Members of your church
only? What about everyone else? Do you care if they all starve or suffer? Why not cut to the
chase. Why not strive for an equal world? Why not be egalitarian? Could you let go of the
desire to make infinite money and embrace economics and business with the purpose of
helping all people live a healthy thriving happy life? That is Egalitarian Economics. VN:F

freezer buildings to store more ice cream. I live as close as I can to ice cream suppliers. I may
build my own Ice cream factory. I don’t care how my actions effect anyone or anything else in

care if I kill people to get ice cream- unless I am going to get caught and go to jail for it – and
only then because I probably won’t get enough ice cream in jail.
Now imagine Mr. Ice Cream is your next door neighbor. He would be one wierd flipping
neighbor. You know this neighbor is a totally obsessed sociopath with a neurotic and
dangerous fixation on the acquisition of ice cream. You a little worried he might do something
horrible to you or your family in order to feed his ice cream habit, but you figure the laws

to jail. He will never be stopped from his ravenous Ice Cream acquisition habits. Taking risking
highly damaging action to get more ice cream is now simply a small calculated risk for Mr. Ice

no real deterrent because the maximum ice cream penalty is only a few pints. So Mr. Ice Cream

more Ice Cream.
Maybe you start thinking that Mr. Ice Cream needs to be reigned in. So you might try to ask
your law makers to try and control Mr. Ice Cream. Then you discover your law makers are all
ice cream addicts getting fed regularly by Mr. Ice Cream. Now your world is a nightmare.
Welcome to the USA in 2012. Welcome to modern capitalist democracy.

lunatic. They are an obsessed, scary, crazy individual. A healthy human being has a diverse

world around them. A healthy human being is capable of emotion. Only a really messed up

anything else. And yet, our world today is controlled by really messed up demented crazy
entities exactly like Mr. Ice Cream: corporations.
We are talking about “for profit” corporations. A “for profit” corporation exists for one thing

Why Egalitarian?
September 11, 2012
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
I practice what I would call: non-violent egalitarian facilitation. It has become the only type of
facilitation I am really interested in. Egalitarian Means Equal Power The basic premise I
operate by at all times while facilitating is that every person in the room is 100% equal in
power- including the facilitator. Working from this single premise, every step of facilitation
flows from that foundation.
The first step in egalitarian facilitation is to ask, “Who would like to volunteer to facilitate this
meeting?” From that point forward, every decision in how the meeting proceeds is ultimately
up to this group of 100% equal people. The facilitator merely facilitates egalitarian group
decisions to go as smoothly as possible. Non-Violent Means Consensus Equal power of
individuals does not eliminate the possibility of violence in group decision making. To clearly
understand violence in group decision making, just ask this question: Is it theoretically
possible for this group to decide to commit violence upon one of the people in this group? Does
the group decision making method allow that possibility?
In any group where decision are made by “voting” violence is easily imaginable. If enough
people vote “kill Joe” then Joe could be killed.
The only group decision making process that by definition makes violence and domination
impossible is consensus. The definition of consensus is that all members of the group have an
equal power in the process and all members must “consent” to all group decisions. Minimal
consent is simply to “not object” to a group decision. The only way for a group using consensus
to commit violence on a member is either to break the “equal power” principle or do it with the
members consent. It’s All About Power Non violent communication and egalitarianism is all
about power. Once you learn to see power dynamics in groups, it begins to stand out like a
glowing radioactive statue in the room. I’ve spent so much time thinking about it, working
with it, and working to be acutely sensitive to it while facilitating meetings of a broad breath of
activists in the Occupy movement, I am now acutely sensitive to power dynamics in all my
human relationships.
I have discovered about myself that I simply have no interest in power dynamics. I have no
interest in having power over other people and I certainly have no interest in others having
power over me. It is rather incredible how often power dynamics emerge in every human
interaction, whether it is one on one or in a group of some sort. It doesn’t matter if it is a social
setting or a “meeting” setting. Power is always a dynamic I find worth paying attention to. Feel
That Discomfort? That May Be A Power Dynamic. If you are in a group environment and you
feel a strong discomfort, then you might consider looking at it carefully. You may discover
power is a huge factor in that discomfort.
If you feel a discomfort, then you should move so you no longer feel it. If you are in a group
situation and feel a huge discomfort- and you are not moving to relieve it- why not? What is
stopping you? Most likely, something or someone is stopping you – and that is power! Maybe
do a little internal check in, does this thing or person genuinely have power over you – and you
are ok with that – or are you just being submissive? Maybe allow yourself to day dream, what
would happen if I moved at this moment in a way to try an relieve my discomfort? It might be
to say something, move to another place in the room, or to simply walk out. If you can imagine
the perfect movement for relieving your discomfort, then I say go for it. What’s the worst that
can happen? In my experience, the worst that can happen is for you to sit there uncomfortable
and dominated by some power dynamic.
Power is a player in all human interactions. If you want power to be equal and non-violent,
then you have to be attentive to it in your interactions. You must be watchful and mindful of
your power over yourself but just as mindful of others who might be tempted to submit to
you. Don’t give people power but also don’t take power just because it might be offered.
As I do this, I discover that when you refuse to unbalance power in your human relationships,
when you absolutely reject any desire to have power over other people’s lives, then you find
yourself in this amazing place of peace and clarity. You do what is right for you at all times.
You ask of your friends to always give you the space you need when you need it – and by
following this – you rarely find you need space when your friends need your help.
I find I am present for my friends. I don’t feel compelled to tell them what I think about what
they are doing. I don’t feel any need to influence their behavior. When you remove power from
a human relationship, what is left? If you don’t have power over your friends and they don’t
have power over you then what is left to determine what each of you do while you are together?
If you think about a human relationship, every moment you are with someone, you might say
that you are at every moment either taking, giving, receiving, offering, or waiting. If you
remove acts of power over your friend, then you eliminate “taking”. Imagine saying to your
friend, “I will take nothing from you. I will only accept that which you offer me. I will offer you
things, but I will never force anything upon you. You may have whatever I offer you and leave
whatever you do not want.” And if your friend were to ask you, “Why are you doing this? Why
are you so generous to give, offer, and take nothing?” The only answer that remains for me is,
“Because it makes me happy. I offer and give to you because it makes me happy. I accept some
things you offer me because it makes me happy. I won’t accept anything I don’t want. I take
nothing forcibly from you, neither your time, attention, or anything else, because I find no joy
in domination and theft.” To me, that is a healthy human relationship. To me that is love.
So you might say, I believe in non-violent egalitarian relationships, because that is what love is.
VN:F [1.9.22_1171]

What has the Occupy Movement Accomplished?
September 22, 2012
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
What has the Occupy Movement Accomplished? Is the movement dead? These seem to be
questions people often like to discuss these days. Here is my answer:
Before the Occupy movement, I lived my life. I went home at the end of my day. And when I
looked at the politics in the United States, I said to myself, “Our democracy is broken. It is
completely controlled by money. The elections are controlled by money. Most of media which
works very hard to brainwash people into how to vote and who to vote for is controlled by the
same money that controls the elections. Participating in this farce of a democracy is practically
pointless. The whole thing is totally messed up. It needs way more than my vote. This broken
system needs a massive overhaul.” Or some such thing. I would think this and I would shrug
because I felt utterly alone and powerless against this fundamental messedupedness of our
system.
Once in a while I would talk about way money corrupts our political system with friends. And
they would agree. And they would agree that there really isn’t anything for us to do. Once in a
while I might encounter someone who said, “Get involved, vote, or run for office if you want to
change things.” But I could not stomach playing by the horrible rules our system has in place.
I didn’t want to be a part of this system that is so broken and corrupt. So I just lived my life and
shook my head at the two dominant corporate parties and the corporate approved issues they
and the media told everyone were the hot button issues. No one wanted to discuss the real hot
button issues, that our system is corrupted by money and both parties are utterly controlled by
it. Nope, the real issues were taboo.
Then the Occupy Movement happened. People started coming out of the wood work echoing
my deepest feelings of discontent about the fundamental workings of our supposed democracy.
They began naming the true and taboo issue: Money in politics. Money controls our politics.
This is no longer a healthy democracy. This is a corporatocracy. And these people came
together and said, “We want to work together in a way the fundamentally goes against the
power struggles that define our culture. We are going to organize using a leaderless consensus
process. And we are going to put our bodies on the line to fight for the change our democracy
needs.”
When it fully sank in that there were people out there who felt the same discontent as myself
and then I learned how they wanted to work together, I suddenly knew I finally had a place to
bring my energy, skills, and passion for helping this country repair some of its deepest
problems. I left my home, I found a place where others like me would gather- and where I
believed we could all work together in a beautiful way for change.
What has the Occupy movement accomplished? It let those of us who are fed up with our
broken democracy know we are not alone. It let us all know there are others out there willing
to devote time and sacrifice in order to build a better world- and willing to do so
without compromise. “What don’t we want? Incremental change! When don’t we want it? 10
years from now!”
What has the Occupy movement accomplished? It got me out of my house. It introduced me to
an army of amazing friends. Over the last year we have enjoyed thousands of direct actions
designed to directly attack the root causes of our failing democracy. We are gut punching the
system. Have we knocked out money in politics yet? Hardly. Have some people gone back
home? Sure. But these are all the wrong questions.
A better question might be, “Has the Occupy movement gotten the money out of politics yet?”
The answer is of course no. But the next statement is not, “Ok Occupy failed, what’s on TV
now?” The next question needs to be, “How can I help get the money out of politics?” or “What
am I doing to get the money out of politics?”
You are debating the wrong question when you debate the accomplishments of the Occupy
movement or of this guy or that guy or this party or that party. Focus on the problems the
Occupy Movement was trying to address: money in politics, poverty, student loan debt,
healthcare. Are those problems fixed? NO! So what are you going to do about it?
When you allow the media or another person to define the question, then you allow them to
shift the focus of the debate.
We have a big problem in our supposedly “greatest democracy on earth”. Our democracy is
corrupted and destroyed by the power of money. Do something about it. If you don’t think the
Occupy movement is the place for you, then find your place. Don’t be one of the people living
your safe comfortable life and sit at home saying, “Ha, you guys couldn’t fix the problems. I
told you so.”
If you aren’t helping fix the problems, then you are part of the problem. Don’t sit around
waiting for the Occupy movement to succeed or fail at fixing the problems you know are there.
Get up out of your chair and join the struggle. May 2013 Update I have taken a bold new step to
try and address some of the problems in our society: I am running for hospital commissioner
for East Jefferson County Washington. I am running because I have the skills and knowledge
necessary to be an outstanding member of our hospital board. I am also running because as
commissioner, I know I can help our hospital district repair many of flaws in our healthcare
system locally and help influence repairs on a wider scale. To read more about my campaign
and to watch videos from debates, please visit: http://readyforhealthcare.org. VN:F

Got Focus?
September 24, 2012
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
Can you sit and stare at a single point for 45 minutes?
If so- awesome!
Try this focused work meditation now:
Accept in your mind, you are meditating, not working at this moment. It is the excercise that
matters- not how “productive” you are during this. Meditate for 1-5 minutes. Sit somewhere
where you are surrounded by shit loads of work. Either home or at work or wherever. Meditate
1 minute. Now focus your attention on this question:
What are the possible tasks I could do now? Make a list of the top 3-5 possible tasks then stop.
Meditate 1 minute. Now meditate upon this question: Which of these top 3-5 tasks would be
the most satisfying to have completely and utterly done? Choose that one. Now the fun part.
This task is now your single point of focus. Focus your attention on doing this task. This task is
like the point in space you are staring at when doing the visual focus meditation. There is no
rush. There are no rules. The only rule is you must keep attention on this point. You can
expand your attention to include other things. You can move your body around and do
whatever you want- but you cannot do other work. You don’t have to make fast progress on the
task. You simply must keep your attention on it. You cannot choose a different task to work
on. This task is the only task you can pay attention to. This task is the only task you are
permitting yourself to pay attention to or work on. When you are done with the task, meditate
for 2 minutes. Now choose another task and repeat. Try doing this for an entire morning. I
find it flipping amazing.

True Self False Self
December 29, 2012
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
A conscious life is not a simple thing. A conscious life is not a single definitive entity. We are
subtle. We exist in layers.
The most apparent and obvious layer is our false self. You might call this the egoic self or our
mask. This layer is the character we might describe to others when sharing our life story.
What we like. What we fear. What we want. What we did. What we hope to do. Most people
think this is who they are. This layer contains most of our feelings, emotions, pains, joys. This
layer contains all our beliefs and categories with which we define our existence. Most people
live the majority of their lives in this layer- thinking it is them. Most, but I suspect no one lives
all their life in this layer- since many types of experiences and events will crack or disintegrate
this layer- if only briefly. When this layer disintegrates, we experience our subtle layer, our
true self.
Our true self is infinite, mysterious, glorious, fascinating, energizing, playful, curious, peaceful…
I can hardly claim to know it well enough to describe it well. It is like an amazing friend you
might know, who inspires you and amazes you- but whom you feel unqualified to adequately
describe.
Your true self is what is left when everything else is destroyed- which happens sometimes.
Once in a while, our world tends to fall apart. Relationships end. Death happens. Accidents
happen. Shit happens. Once in a while, shit happens with such ferociousness and suddenness
that it obliterates everything we thought we were, everything we thought life was about. If this
destruction is only partial, if it merely disintegrates a portion of our world- then we will likely
just experience extraordinary pain, sadness, anxiety. We will most likely cry a lot during such
an experience. If on the other hand, the change in our life is dramatic enough – or if we allow
the cracks to fully penetrate and crumble the false self, then the suffering instantly ends, and
we experience a peace, a clarity, a joy. This is the true self when it is able to surface and
experience existence without the false lenses of our egoic self.
Most people have numerous experiences in their life where they glimpse the true self. You
probably can remember moments in your life where suddenly you saw the world differently,
where you felt an expanding peace and joy, where life felt vast and endlessly full of possibilities
and excitement. You may have had experiences of extreme tragedy or loss which somehow
took you through feelings of utter misery and sadness- only to then bring you to a feeling of
infinite peace and acceptance. If you haven’t had much of such experiences as an adult, you
doubtless had them while a child. VN:F [1.9.22_1171]

Who We Are. What We Are Not.
March 15, 2013
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
If you are like me, you are a human- and so this may apply to you. If you are not human and
reading this, please drop me a line, let’s hang out some time.
For me, one of the greatest revelations of my journey to understand life, consciousness,
happiness, and all that good stuff – has been a better understanding of who I am. In fact, I find
one of the most powerful and infinitely rewarding questions to meditate deeply upon is “Who
am i?”.
The question on “Who am I?” is critically more important than “What do I want?”. In fact, I
find as you begin to truly investigate who you are, you may realize that is always the more
important question than “What do I want?” You realize this, because you are not a singular
entity. You are at least two and perhaps many more than that.
You are not a singular entity. You may have one body and one brain, but you are not a simple
single thing, “you”. If you are walking down a street and you see a giant neon sign that says,
“You want a Pizza right now!”, would you always want a Pizza? Of course not. Maybe never.
Maybe sometimes. Would you when seeing this sign think to yourself, “That sign is a part of
me. That sign is a part of who I am as a person.”? I hope not. That sign is not a part of you.
That sign is a thing you are experiencing in the world.
What about when that neon sign is not on the street but inside your mind? When you have a
loud voice in your head say, “I want pizza!” perhaps accompanied with images of tasty pizza’s
like in a commercial, do you always say to yourself, “I want a pizza.”? Perhaps you do. Most
people do. But you are jumping the gun. Because most people when they hear a voice in their
heads say something and or display images of wants, they think to themselves, “That voice is a
part of me. That voice is a part of who I am as a person.” This is a fallacy. That voice is real. It
is as real as the neon sign on the street. Yet, that voice is simply a thing- just like the neon sign
on the street. It is merely a thing in the world you are encountering on your journey. To
believe that thing is you- is to trap yourself- to enslave yourself to something.
You have a body and a brain. This doesn’t mean you have to accept that everything contained
in this body and brain is you. Your body and brain are just things, objects made of matter and
energy. You inhabit them, but they are not you. When you die, your body and brain will
remain, but you will be gone. Your body may yearn for things, it may give you physical
sensations of craving- like a rumbling stomach when you think of pizza- but you are not that
craving. You are the thing that is aware of the craving. You are the thing that chooses to seek
pizza or not. You are the boss- you just may not know it or act like it all the time.
Who are you? This is the deepest richest question you can ever ask. I encourage you to ask it.
For the more you ask it. The more you understand the difference between the true you and all
the other stuff in your body and mind, you more you can begin to ask the truly interesting
questions of life- like “What do I feel? What do I see? What do I want?”. And then the very
exciting follow up question, “What could I do?” and “What shall I do?”. But if you skip the first
question, the fundamental question of “who are you?”, you may find yourself living your life
seeking things you don’t truly want.


I tweeted yesterday that sometimes subtle stifling habits are a greater challenge than horrible
addictions. I think this is true in a way, because horrible addictions are much more visible to
you and others. With horrible addictions, you at least have physical consequences and often
some amount of positive peer pressure to help remind you of the healthy path. On the other
hand, subtle stifling habits, you are often truly on your own. You may find it very lonely to say
no to activities that you know are unhealthy for you, but everyone around you considers totally
fine- like eating certain things, watching tv, drinking to excess, or even just unsatisfying social
events. You may know 100% inside, “I don’t want to do this.” yet you do it, because it is a habit-
perhaps one reenforced by social expectations. I find such habits a constantly recurring
challenge.
Yesterday, I was able to snap one such habit- and the way I did it I am going to remember. I
will likely have to use it again.
I had acquired this habit of watching a couple television programs in bed before going to sleep.
I would hop into be around 9:30 or 10 and then watch one or two programs and possibly stay up
until midnight before sleeping. A very common activity for many people I am sure. The thing
is, this habit was forcing me to break another routine I really loved- getting up at 6 am to
meditate and start my day before most of my household. I had established and maintained the
early rising routine for several months, but finally my tv watching habit at night was causing a
crisis of sleep deprivation. I then realized I was somewhat sleepy all the time and I knew
without a doubt, that was unhealthy. So I started letting myself sleep in to 7:30 or 8- which
resulted in me rising with most everyone else. Often I wouldn’t have time to meditate before
my day got going. Before I knew it, I was unhappy with the general rhythm of my days.
This pattern was really frustrating- until finally one day- after a good nights sleep, I did a nice
long meditation. Towards the end of the meditation this crisis of daily patterns rose up in my
consciousness- and I finally looked at it head on. It is amazing how sometimes you just need to
turn the headlights directly on the issue so you can see what is what. A part of me did not want
to look at this problem. A part of me just did not want to consider the possibility that I might
not watch these really good fun television shows. But I honestly looked at what was happening.
Did I truly enjoy those television shows? Did I truly value watching those shows more than my
amazing early morning routine? As I reflected upon this, I concluded that it was not as simple
as saying to myself, “No tv shows for me ever.” Although I think this is what a part of me was
fearing I would say. Rather I concluded, “The television shows are not more important than my
early mornings.” This is 100% true. This meant, at a bare minimum, I would not start
watching any television show after 9:15 at night. I would absolutely not watch anything that
would not be done by 10 pm. I wanted to make a commitment to my body that at 10 pm, if I
was tired, I could sleep. I would not do something like watch TV that kept me over stimulated
and up forever.
This is where it got interesting for me. I had that train of thought above during my morning
meditation. But I was not 100% sure I could actually keep that promise. I honestly thought
through the reasoning and thought it was sound, but I am not a person who rigidly disciplines
myself. If I feel an incredible craving to do something, I sometimes just allow myself to do it. I
am kind of an inner anarchist like that. (I prefer to operate by inner consensus). So I wasn’t
sure at 10pm yesterday night I would not watch the same few shows I’ve been watching lately.
So I went off to work and continued my day.
Here’s the thing I did do- thoughout my day, I often reflected back upon my morning
meditation and the reasoning. All day, every once in a while, I reflected upon that same
reasoning, I wondered what I would do when the moments arrived at night, I wondered what it
would be like to not watch tv, I wondered what would I do instead. I wondered how my
housemates might react if they asked me to watch something. This reflecting upon my decision
and plan really helped me to prepare myself for the moment of truth that was to come. And
when the moment did come, it was a breeze. I simply said, “I am not watching anything
tonight.” I didn’t know what else to do, so I went and meditated for 45 minutes. Then I went to
bed, read a little bit, and slept. At 6 am my alarm went off and I got up, fresh and happy to start
my day.


I’ve joined these two posts together for this reason: They are about the same thing. A thing
inside me wanted to watch television-but this thing is not me. The true me is the feeling
thinking entity that wakes up during meditation. This true me was not happy. This true me
was feeling totally frustrated by this thing that was taking over my behavior when I was tired
and preventing the type of daily routine I knew would make the true me happy. It is like
having a noisy obnoxious neighbor that has a key to your house and just barges in whenever
they feel like it. You feel sort of abused by this thing. Yet, all you need to do is face the problem
honestly. Tell the neighbor, you have to knock- or perhaps I’ll let you know if I want to spend
time with you. Then you change the locks and move on. You are in charge. You are what
matters. The true you. Get to know yerself. VN:F [1.9.22_1171]

Life as an Uncollapsed Wave Function
March 19, 2013
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
“You are a superhero- a superposition hero.”
The electron chooses between the two slits only when one of us is watching. If no one is
watching- it does not choose. If no one is watching, then it replies “undecided.”
Consciousness is like firing an electron at uneven double slits. One slit one size, the other slit
bigger. Still while unobserved, the electron will not choose. It continues to reply “undecided”.
Yet, if watched, the electron will now choose- and with uneven double slits, it may choose one
75% of the time and the other 25%- relative to the different sizes of the slits. With extremely
uneven slits, perhaps it will choose 99.9% one and just .1% the other. Yet, when unobserved, it
will continue to reply – “undecided.”
We might call out to this indecisive electron, “These double slits are so far different- why
continue to pretend you may choose the unlikely one- when 99.9% of the time you will choose
the other?” The electrons unspoken reply, “I am undecided- because I can. I am free.”
Let us fire a single electron at the uneven double slits. Through which slit will it pass? Can we
predict it? Can we know? No. We cannot predict it or know. We can state a probability based
upon conditions, but nothing in science will ever reveal what that electron will choose- for that
is exactly what the electron does- it chooses- when it is forced to choose- it chooses- freely.
When asked why this path, again the only reply can be, “I chose this path because I chose this
path.”
Our human will is like that electron. In moments of great decisions, perhaps it even comes
down to single such electrons. Often we are torn between uneven choices- what we are
compelled to do by habit, emotion, or other forces- and what we wish to do in our hearts. One
choice is easy- the path of least resistance. The other choice defies probability. What then
happens?
Do you 99% of the time submit to the habit, emotion, or other force that does not come from
your heart of hearts? Or do you often push the electrons of your neural nets through the less
likely path- via your power of free will- and choose the harder path, the path of greater
resistence?
When the bravest acts of life happen, and we ask “Why? Why did you choose to make such a
sacrifice? Why did you choose to take the harder path? Why did you not follow the more likely
and far easier path?” The reply is eerily similar to that electron. It is, “Because I am free to
choose- and I chose what I wanted- not what I felt compelled to do.”
Our conscious mind is that undecided electron. We exist moment to moment as uncollapsed
probability waves. An electron will take the 75% easier path 75% of the time- when forced to
choose. A person can ignore the easiest path- 100% of the time- far outside the realm of
chance- for a human consciousness is a living electron in uncollapsed probability state. It does
not collapse itself randomly upon a choice. It chooses how it collapses- or it is at least capable
of doing so- and like the electron, when we do so, we do so because we have embraced our
freedom. VN:F [1.9.22_1171]
