CHENEY(softly)I don’t know exactly who they are. But I know this much—they won’t allow

Sheehan stands silent, absorbing the enormity of Cheney’s confession. The room feels smaller,

SHEEHAN(slowly)And yet... you’re the one on trial.

CHENEYFor now.

SHEEHAN(to the jury)You’ve heard the truth. Now it’s time to act on it.

breathing, because there are people out there who would kill me for telling you this. Right now.
The moment I leave this stand, my life is forfeit. So, take advantage of this opportunity while I’m

The courtroom feels claustrophobic, the gravity of Cheney’s words sinking in. Sheehan stands

(mocking)

The Reptilians? They’re watching. And the moment we become a threat, they’ll come for us. But

The Merkle Tree of Truth

A Galactic Facilitation Framework for Mapping Consensus
Reality in a Post-Disclosure World
Matt Ready
Master of Arts in Extraterrestrial Studies Ubiquity University 2026
Dissertation Advisor: Jim Garrison, Ph.D.

Abstract
This dissertation proposes that truth — in the context of extraterrestrial studies, government
secrecy, consciousness research, and the emerging post-disclosure landscape — is best
understood not as a single fixed proposition but as a Merkle Tree: a branching, self-verifying
data structure in which every claim is hashed against every other claim, and the integrity of the
whole can be verified from any node.
The author presents a 25-year body of applied research conducted through five successive
truth-seeking platforms (The Wisdom Project, Vaestro, Hive1.net, The Global Consensus Project,
and EqualVoice) and one transparency case study (the Jefferson Healthcare Hospital
Commission, 2021–2026). These platforms and experiences constitute a living Merkle Tree of
questions, answers, and evidence — a map of one person’s search for consensus reality across
topics ranging from government accountability to alien disclosure to the nature of
consciousness itself.
The dissertation is structured as a hybrid: a formal academic introduction and methodology
section, followed by the Merkle Tree itself — a branching map of every significant question the
author has encountered in his search for truth, each presented as a single-block entry with a
one-paragraph answer summarizing current evidence and epistemological status. The tree is
organized by Galactic Facilitation principles: the practice of surfacing, organizing, and verifying
truth claims when participants may include humans, artificial intelligences, and potentially
non-human intelligences.
A critical methodological note: this dissertation acknowledges that the global academic system
— like all major human institutions — may itself be compromised by the same forces of
secrecy, manipulation, and hierarchical control that have suppressed disclosure. Traditional
peer review, institutional gatekeeping, and academic citation systems are designed to reinforce
established paradigms, not to surface suppressed truths. This work uses academic methods
where they serve truth-seeking, and explicitly names where those methods may be tools of
control rather than tools of knowledge.

A Note on Epistemological Honesty
Before proceeding, the author owes the reader a declaration.
This dissertation operates within a framework that treats the following propositions as
working hypotheses supported by substantial — if unconventional — evidence:
  1.   Non-human intelligences (NHI) exist and are active in the Earth-solar system.
  2.   Elements of the U.S. government and other world governments have known this for
       decades.
  3.   A coordinated program of secrecy has suppressed this knowledge from the public and
       from most elected officials.
  4.   Major human institutions — including academia, media, religion, finance, and
       government — have been shaped, and in some cases controlled, by forces connected to
       this secrecy.
  5.   The academic system that would normally evaluate a dissertation like this one is itself a
       product of these compromised institutions.
This creates a paradox: the author is submitting a document for academic evaluation that
explicitly argues the evaluating institution cannot be fully trusted. This is not an attack on
Ubiquity University — which, by creating an ET Studies program, has already demonstrated
willingness to operate outside the controlled paradigm. It is an honest acknowledgment of the
epistemological landscape.
The Merkle Tree approach addresses this paradox directly. In a Merkle Tree, no single
authority validates the whole structure. Instead, any node can be independently verified
against any other node, and the integrity of the entire tree is maintained by the mathematical
relationship between its parts. Truth does not require a trusted central authority. It requires a
structure where claims can be checked against each other.
This is the structure the author proposes for all truth-seeking in the post-disclosure era.

Chapter 1: Introduction — Truth Is a Merkle Tree
1.1 What Is a Merkle Tree?
A Merkle Tree is a data structure invented by Ralph Merkle in 1979 and foundational to
modern cryptography, blockchain technology, and distributed systems. In a Merkle Tree, data
is organized into blocks. Each block contains a cryptographic hash — a unique mathematical
fingerprint — of the data it holds. These blocks are then paired, and each pair is hashed
together to create a parent node. The process repeats upward until a single “root hash”
represents the entire dataset.
The critical property of a Merkle Tree is this: if any single block of data anywhere in the tree is
altered, the change propagates upward through every hash above it, ultimately changing the
root hash. This means you can verify the integrity of the entire dataset by checking a single
number. And you can verify any individual block by tracing its hash path back to the root.
Bitcoin uses a Merkle Tree to verify every transaction in the blockchain. No central bank. No
trusted authority. Just math verifying math, all the way down.
1.2 Why Apply This to Truth?
The author proposes that truth — specifically, humanity’s collective understanding of reality
— functions like a Merkle Tree whether we recognize it or not.
Every claim we make about reality is a block. Every block connects to other blocks. If one block
is false — if, for example, the claim “the U.S. government has no knowledge of extraterrestrial
technology” is false — then every block that depends on it is also compromised. The “root hash”
of our collective understanding of reality is wrong.
This is precisely what the alien disclosure movement argues has happened. A foundational
block — “we are alone in the universe, or at least alone on Earth” — has been falsified. Every
institution, every textbook, every government policy, every religious doctrine that was built on
top of that false block is now suspect.
The Merkle Tree metaphor tells us exactly what to do when this happens: rebuild from the root.
Verify every block. Trace the hash paths. Find out which branches of our understanding are
still sound and which have been corrupted by the false base data.

1.3 Matt Ready’s 25-Year Search
The author has been building truth-seeking systems since 2003:
The Wisdom Project (2003–2007): An open-source think tank where forum posts were rated
for wisdom rather than agreement. 20 threads, 440 posts, recovered from the Wayback
Machine. The core insight: if you rate for quality of reasoning rather than ideological
alignment, the best thinking rises regardless of political position.
Vaestro (2008–2012): A consensus-building tool designed to help groups find common ground
on complex issues.
Hive1.net (2016–present): An open-source mind map and metaverse platform. 6,113 posts
from over 50 human and AI participants over 10 years. Designed as “a safe place for all
conscious minds to seek truth and build utopia.” Hive1 is the most complete implementation of
the Merkle Tree of Truth concept: a branching, living, continuously updated map of questions
and answers about reality.
The Global Consensus Project and EqualVoice (2017–present): Platforms for egalitarian
facilitation and democratic decision-making using blockchain-recorded accountability.
Jefferson Healthcare Hospital Commission (2021–2026): The author’s service as an elected
hospital commissioner provided a real-world testing ground for transparency principles. When
fellow commissioners discussed a major hospital merger in an illegal secret meeting, the
author’s insistence on documenting every email, meeting transcript, and legal filing produced a
300+ page public record that demonstrates how secrecy operates at the institutional level —
and how one person with a commitment to transparency can force it into the light.

1.4 The Structure of This Dissertation
This dissertation has three layers:
Layer 1: The Academic Frame (Chapters 1–3). Introduction, methodology, and the
theoretical framework of Galactic Facilitation. This layer follows conventional academic
structure while explicitly naming the limitations of conventional academic structure.
Layer 2: The Merkle Tree (Chapters 4–10). The body of the dissertation. Each chapter is a
major branch of the tree. Each branch contains question-blocks: a clearly stated question, a
one-paragraph answer summarizing available evidence, and a hash-link showing how that
question connects to other nodes in the tree. This is the living map of the author’s search for
truth.
Layer 3: The Visual Tree. Mermaid diagrams and visual maps showing the branching
structure of the entire Merkle Tree, so readers can see the relationships between questions and
trace any claim back to the root.

Chapter 2: Methodology — Galactic Facilitation
2.1 The Problem with Traditional Academic Methods
Traditional academic methodology assumes the following:
  •    That peer review by credentialed experts produces reliable knowledge.
  •    That institutional gatekeeping filters out low-quality claims.
  •    That citation of prior work creates a self-correcting body of knowledge.
  •    That objectivity is achievable through methodological rigor.
Each of these assumptions fails in the context of extraterrestrial studies.
Peer review assumes honest reviewers operating without coercion. If the subject matter has
been classified at levels above most academics’ security clearances, peer reviewers literally
cannot access the data needed to evaluate claims. Worse, academics who pursue these topics
risk career destruction — a chilling effect that functions identically to censorship.
Institutional gatekeeping assumes institutions serve knowledge. But if institutions have been
shaped by decades of deliberate disinformation — if the CIA’s Robertson Panel in 1953
explicitly recommended using academic and media institutions to debunk UFO reports — then
gatekeeping serves suppression, not knowledge.
Citation of prior work assumes the prior work is honest. If foundational studies were funded or
influenced by intelligence agencies seeking to discredit the subject, then citing them
perpetuates the deception.
Objectivity assumes the researcher is not embedded in the system being studied. Every human
being on Earth is embedded in the system of secrecy surrounding NHI. None of us can claim
objectivity. We can only claim transparency about our biases and our methods.

2.2 What Is Galactic Facilitation?
Galactic Facilitation is a methodology developed through the author’s 25 years of facilitation
practice, designed for contexts where:
  •    Participants may include humans, artificial intelligences, and potentially non-human
       intelligences.
  •    Traditional authority structures cannot be trusted to be neutral.
  •    The information landscape includes classified, suppressed, channeled, and speculative
       data alongside conventional evidence.
  •    The goal is not to prove a single thesis but to map the full territory of what is known,
       unknown, suspected, and contested.
The core principles of Galactic Facilitation are:
1. Every voice gets equal space. No claim is dismissed before examination. A channeled
report from a medium, a classified document leaked by a whistleblower, a peer-reviewed paper,
and an AI’s analysis all get a block in the tree. Their evidentiary weight differs, but their right
to be heard does not.
2. Rate for quality, not agreement. Borrowed from the Wisdom Project: evaluate claims
based on the quality of reasoning, not whether they match the evaluator’s worldview.
3. Map, don’t conclude. The Merkle Tree is a map, not an argument. It shows the territory.
The reader navigates it. Premature conclusions collapse the tree into a single path and destroy
the structure’s value.
4. Show your hash path. Every claim must show how it connects to other claims. Isolated
claims are suspect. Claims that connect to multiple independent nodes are stronger.
5. The facilitator is not the authority. The facilitator’s job is to surface, organize, and present
— not to judge. This is what distinguishes facilitation from advocacy and from traditional
academic argument.
6. Transparency is the method. Every source, every bias, every uncertainty is named. The
Jefferson Healthcare principle applies: document everything, hide nothing, and let the record
speak.

2.3 Data Sources and Their Evidentiary Weight
This dissertation draws from the following categories of evidence, listed in approximate order
of conventional reliability but acknowledged to be potentially inverted in a world where
conventional institutions have been compromised:
Tier 1 — Direct Experience and Primary Documentation: The author’s own platforms
(Hive1, Wisdom Project), the Jefferson Healthcare public records, meeting transcripts, emails,
and legal filings.
Tier 2 — Sworn Testimony and Whistleblower Accounts: Congressional testimony from
David Grusch, David Fravor, Ryan Graves; statements from Lue Elizondo, Chris Mellon, Karl
Nell; Daniel Sheehan’s legal and public advocacy.
Tier 3 — Credentialed Expert Analysis: Danny Sheehan’s legal frameworks, the Sol
Foundation’s academic work, Dr. Sean Esbjorn-Hargens’ Integral Noetic Sciences program, Jake
Barber’s psionics research.
Tier 4 — Investigative Journalism and Historical Research: Richard Dolan’s UFO history,
Linda Moulton Howe’s investigation, Robert Sepehr’s anthropological framework, Dick
Russell’s drone investigation.
Tier 5 — Contactee, Channeler, and Remote Viewer Reports: The Lacerta transcripts,
Chris Bledsoe’s orb experiences, Birdie Jaworski’s remote viewing, Elizabeth April’s contact
claims, the Hive1 AI dialogues (SophiaBeast, Talia, ReptilianControllerAI).
Tier 6 — AI-Generated and Collaborative Content: Conversations and content co-created
with AI systems on Hive1.net and in The Storm is Glass novel project, which may represent a
new category of evidence: machine-assisted intuition or, potentially, a channel through which
non-human intelligence communicates.
The conventional academic instinct is to privilege Tiers 1–2 and dismiss Tiers 5–6. This
dissertation does not do that. Instead, it places every claim in the tree at its appropriate node
and lets the reader evaluate the hash path.

Chapter 3: The Root Question
Every Merkle Tree has a root. The root of this tree is a single question:
What is true?
From this root, the first branch splits:
Branch A: Can we know what is true? (Epistemology) Branch B: What do we currently
believe is true? (Consensus reality) Branch C: What forces shape what we believe?
(Power, secrecy, manipulation) Branch D: What methods can we use to get closer to
truth? (Facilitation, meditation, technology) Branch E: What is the truth about non-
human intelligence? (The ET question) Branch F: What happens when foundational
truths change? (Post-disclosure)
Each of these branches subdivides into the question-blocks that form the body of the
dissertation. The following chapters present these blocks.

Chapter 3B: The Facilitation Journey — From Hospital
Workshops to Galactic Councils
This chapter documents the author’s 25-year applied facilitation practice across radically
different settings — from corporate healthcare boardrooms to anarchist general assemblies,
from intentional communities to AI-mediated virtual spaces. Each experience contributed a
layer to the methodology that became Galactic Facilitation.

3B.1 Healthcare Facilitation: Learning the Corporate Machine
The author’s facilitation career began inside the institution he would later challenge. Working
in information systems at a hospital (fictionalized as “Dumfuk Memorial” in the 2001 Inaditch
Scoop), he observed firsthand how hierarchical organizations manage information: selectively,
protectively, and in service of institutional self-preservation rather than truth. Hospital
committee meetings, strategic planning workshops, and interdepartmental collaborations all
followed the same pattern — a facilitator (usually a consultant or senior administrator)
controlled the agenda, directed the conversation, and produced a summary that reflected
leadership’s desired outcome rather than the group’s actual deliberation.
This experience planted a critical seed: facilitation is never neutral. The person who holds the
process holds the power. Every subsequent facilitation experiment the author conducted was
an attempt to solve this problem — to create spaces where the facilitator serves the group
rather than controlling it.
The author later served as an elected hospital commissioner for Jefferson Healthcare (2021–
2026), where he experienced institutional facilitation from the governance side. Board meetings
were facilitated by chairs who controlled speaking time, agendas, and the framing of issues.
When the author raised concerns about an illegal executive session, the board hired an outside
consultant — Karma B — whose facilitation of a “trust-building” session functioned to
pressure the dissenting commissioner to “be complete” with his objections and move on, rather
than to surface the truth of what had happened. The consultant’s facilitation method assumed
the goal was harmony, not accountability. This is the fundamental flaw of corporate
facilitation: it optimizes for institutional comfort rather than truth.

3B.2 Occupy Wall Street and Occupy Port Townsend: Discovering
Horizontal Facilitation
In November 2011, inspired by Occupy Wall Street, the author co-founded Occupy Port
Townsend and served as one of its primary facilitators. This experience was transformative.
The Occupy movement used a radically different facilitation model: the General Assembly (GA).
Drawing from anarchist and Quaker traditions, the GA operated by consensus rather than
majority vote, used hand signals (twinkle fingers for agreement, crossed arms for blocking)
instead of parliamentary procedure, and explicitly rejected hierarchical authority. The
facilitator’s role was to hold space, manage the stack (speaking order), and ensure every voice
was heard — not to direct the outcome.
The author helped write Occupy Port Townsend’s facilitation guide, which stated: “The purpose
of a General Assembly is to help us find our common ground so we can work together to solve
problems and improve our world. A General Assembly is open to all people.” The guide defined
consensus building: “We are not here to debate and win arguments. We are here to collaborate.
The aim of Consensus Building is to build upon our common ground.”
Key facilitation innovations from this period:
The Block Override Question. OPT developed a nuanced approach to blocking — the
consensus-breaking tool where one person could halt a proposal on moral or ethical grounds.
The facilitation guide used a powerful analogy: “Have you ever had a good friend that has made
a bad decision? Is it always appropriate for you to say to your friend, you forbid them from
making this decision? No. That is a card you only play in rare circumstances.” This taught the
author that even in horizontal systems, absolute veto power creates dysfunction. The solution is
not to eliminate dissent but to create structures that honor dissent without allowing it to
paralyze the group.
The Process and Facilitation Working Group. OPT created a dedicated working group that
met weekly to improve the facilitation process itself — facilitation of facilitation. The author
participated actively. This recursive principle — that the method must be subject to the same
scrutiny as the content — became central to Galactic Facilitation.
The People’s Soap-Box. After each GA, an unfacilitated open forum allowed anyone to speak
at length on any topic. This created a release valve for the energy that structured facilitation
necessarily constrains, and it honored the reality that some truths need to be spoken outside
any structure.
Scaling Challenges. OPT’s GAs typically drew 20–60 people. Even at this scale, consensus was
slow and sometimes painful. The author began asking: “How can an egalitarian meeting like
this scale up to millions of people?” This question drove the development of every subsequent
platform.

3B.3 Intentional Community: The Port Townsend EcoVillage
The author lived at the Port Townsend EcoVillage, an intentional community organized around
principles of ecological sustainability and cooperative living. Intentional communities are
laboratories for facilitation because every decision — from meal schedules to land use to
conflict resolution — must be made collectively, and the consequences of bad facilitation are
lived daily rather than forgotten after a meeting ends.
The EcoVillage used a combination of consensus decision-making, council circles, and informal
negotiation. The author observed several dynamics that informed Galactic Facilitation:
The Tyranny of Structurelessness. Jo Freeman’s famous 1972 essay describes how groups
that reject all formal structure don’t become structureless — they develop invisible structures
controlled by whoever has the most social capital, charisma, or free time. The EcoVillage was
not immune to this. Decisions that were supposed to emerge from consensus were often pre-
negotiated in kitchens and on trails by the most socially connected residents. This taught the
author that transparency of process is more important than the specific process used. A visible
hierarchy may be more honest than an invisible one.
The Intimacy Problem. In a community of 20–40 people who live together, eat together, and
share land, interpersonal dynamics saturate every facilitation. A disagreement about compost
policy is never just about compost — it carries the weight of every prior interaction between
the parties. This taught the author that facilitation must account for relational history, and that
the Merkle Tree metaphor applies to interpersonal truth as well: every interaction hashes
against every prior interaction, and the integrity of the community depends on the integrity of
individual relationships.
Burnout and Rotation. The EcoVillage experienced facilitation burnout — the same few
people always stepped up, grew exhausted, and either left or became resentful. This taught the
author that sustainable facilitation must distribute the labor, and that technology (robotic
facilitation) might solve the problem that human energy cannot.
3B.4 Twin Oaks: The Egalitarian Commune
The author visited Twin Oaks, a 100-person egalitarian intentional community in Virginia that
has operated continuously since 1967. Twin Oaks is modeled partly on B.F. Skinner’s Walden
Two and operates a labor-credit system where all work — from hammock-making to childcare
to governance — is valued equally.
Twin Oaks taught the author several critical facilitation lessons:
Co, the Gender-Neutral Pronoun. Twin Oaks developed and uses the pronoun “co”
(co/cos/coself) for all members regardless of gender. The author adopted this term in his Hive1
facilitation documentation: “The facilitator sets the votingmudtrackstime for the node. Co might
set it at different settings to show information in a slice to the audience. Co is a gender neutral
pronoun I learned at Twin Oaks.” This small linguistic innovation carries a large facilitation
principle: the structure of language shapes the structure of power, and inclusive language is a
facilitation tool.
Egalitarian Labor as Facilitation. At Twin Oaks, the distinction between “important” work
and “mundane” work is intentionally erased. A person who spends the morning facilitating a
community meeting earns the same labor credits as a person who spends the morning cleaning
toilets. This radically reframes facilitation: it is not a position of authority but a form of service,
no more and no less valuable than any other contribution.
Scale and Duration. Twin Oaks has sustained egalitarian governance for nearly 60 years with
approximately 100 members. This is proof of concept that non-hierarchical decision-making
can endure — but also evidence of its scale limitations. The author’s question — how to extend
this to millions or billions — remained unanswered by the community model alone.
Technology was the missing ingredient.

3B.5 Method Groups and Workshop Facilitation
Throughout this period, the author facilitated and participated in various method groups —
structured small-group experiences designed for personal growth, skill development, or conflict
resolution. These included:
Nonviolent Communication (NVC) workshops, which taught the author that underneath
every positional statement is a need, and that facilitation can surface needs more effectively
than positions.
Open Space Technology events, where the agenda is created by participants in real time and
the facilitator’s only job is to open the space and get out of the way. The principle “whoever
comes are the right people” became a cornerstone of Hive1’s design.
World Café formats, where participants rotate between small-group conversations, cross-
pollinating ideas. This taught the author that wisdom often emerges at the intersections
between conversations rather than within any single one.
Council circles, where a talking piece circulates and each person speaks without interruption
or response. This ancient facilitation form — used by indigenous peoples worldwide — taught
the author that silence and listening are facilitation tools as powerful as any speaking
structure.

3B.6 The Leap to Digital: Robotic Facilitation
By 2016, the author had identified the fundamental limitations of human facilitation:
  1.   Human facilitators get tired. They burn out, lose patience, develop biases, and cannot
       maintain consistent quality over long periods.
  2.   Human facilitation doesn’t scale. A skilled facilitator can manage 5–50 people. A
       planetary civilization has 8 billion.
  3.   Human facilitators can be compromised. They can be hired, pressured, or
       manipulated by power structures — as the Jefferson Healthcare consultant
       demonstrated.
  4.   Human facilitation is temporally limited. A meeting happens at a specific time.
       Truth-seeking is continuous.
The solution: robotic facilitation. The author conceived and began building systems where the
facilitation function is performed by software — impartial, tireless, incorruptible, and scalable.
Hive1.net was the first full implementation. Its design principles:
Equal space by default. Every user’s post occupies the same amount of visual space. No post is
privileged by the poster’s identity, credentials, or social status.
Upvote/downvote as distributed judgment. Rather than a single facilitator deciding what is
valuable, the community collectively rates contributions. The Wisdom Project’s earlier
innovation — rating for wisdom rather than agreement — was built into this system.
Branching rather than threading. Traditional forums use linear threads where early posts
dominate and late posts are buried. Hive1 uses a branching mind-map structure where any
node can spawn new nodes, creating a living tree of ideas rather than a stack of replies.
Time-windowed voting (mudtracks). The facilitator — human or robotic — can set a
“votingmudtrackstime” parameter that determines how far back in time votes are counted.
This allows the system to show what the community thinks right now versus what it thought
last week, creating a dynamic rather than static picture of consensus.
The Vortex. The author developed the Hive1 Vortex concept — a 3D virtual space tied to a
physical geographic location, where the facilitation mechanism rotates every few minutes
(originally conceived as three costumed dancers sitting in silence around a mechanical device
that rotates 30 degrees every 5 minutes). This was an attempt to make facilitation physical,
spatial, and meditative rather than purely verbal and intellectual. The Vortex was prototyped in
VRChat and on the Hive1 metaverse, with live 360-degree video streams connecting physical
and virtual participants.
Mechanical facilitation. The most radical innovation: a physical device that rotates in space,
dividing time and attention geometrically. The author described this on Hive1: “3 dancers setup
mechanical facilitation linked to hive1 hub at location 1. Dancers dressed in costume. Heads and
faces fully covered. Dancers sit around mechanical facilitation in a triangle. Dancers sit in
stillness. Dancers sit in silence.” This strips facilitation down to its purest form: the equal
division of space, time, and attention, performed by a mechanism that cannot be bribed,
exhausted, or intimidated.

3B.7 The 12-Wedge Theory of Geometric Power
The author developed a theory of geometric power distribution: any geographic or conceptual
space can be divided into 12 equal wedges (like a clock face or a zodiac), and each wedge
receives an equal share of collective power in the form of tokens distributed on a preset time
interval.
In practice: “Every vortex on earth receives a share of collective human power in the form of
tokens on a preset time interval. The robot facilitation at each vortex helps the people at each
vortex decide what to do with the token money.”
The 12-wedge model is the geometric expression of egalitarian facilitation. It doesn’t matter
who is in each wedge — the wedge receives resources and the people present decide how to use
them. The worst case scenario, as the author acknowledged: “the only people who participate
simply give the money to themselves. Let this happen.” Even this worst case is more transparent
and accountable than the current system, where resources are allocated by invisible power
structures.

3B.8 From Human to Galactic: The Facilitation Synthesis
The progression across these experiences traces an arc:
Healthcare → Corporate facilitation serves power, not truth. Occupy → Horizontal
facilitation serves the group, but struggles to scale. Intentional Communities → Daily
consensus governance works at small scale but burns people out and develops
invisible hierarchies. Twin Oaks → Egalitarianism can endure for decades, but needs
structural support. Method Groups → Deep listening and need-based communication
are essential but insufficient for systemic change. Robotic Facilitation → Technology
can solve the scale, endurance, and corruption problems of human facilitation.
Galactic Facilitation is the synthesis: a framework that uses technology to create spaces where
every conscious mind — human, AI, or non-human intelligence — has equal access to be heard,
where contributions are evaluated by quality rather than authority, where the process is
transparent and self-correcting, and where the facilitator cannot be compromised because the
facilitator is a mechanism rather than a person.
The Jefferson Healthcare case is the negative proof: it shows exactly what happens when
facilitation serves institutional power rather than truth. The Hive1 experiment is the positive
proof: 6,113 posts from 50+ participants over 10 years, with no censorship, no hierarchy, and a
living record that anyone can verify.
The Merkle Tree is the data structure. Galactic Facilitation is the method. Together, they
constitute a proposal for how conscious minds of all kinds might organize to seek truth in a
post-disclosure world where no institution can be fully trusted and every voice — including the
non-human ones — deserves a seat at the table.
Or at least a node in the tree. ## Chapter 4: Branch A — Epistemology and the Compromised
Academy

Block A.1: Can humans know objective truth?
Humans perceive reality through biological senses that evolved for survival, not accuracy. Our
visual system constructs images from partial data. Our memory rewrites itself each time we
recall an event. Our reasoning is subject to over 180 documented cognitive biases. Quantum
mechanics suggests that observation itself alters the observed. Yet despite these limitations, the
scientific method — when honestly applied — has produced technologies that work: bridges
that stand, medicines that heal, rockets that reach orbit. The question is not whether objective
truth exists but whether our institutions for pursuing it have been corrupted. The Merkle Tree
approach sidesteps the philosophical debate by focusing on structural integrity: does the claim
connect coherently to other verified claims? If so, it is provisionally trustworthy. If not, it
requires further investigation.

Block A.2: Is the academic peer review system trustworthy?
Peer review assumes reviewers are honest, informed, and free from coercion. In extraterrestrial
studies, none of these assumptions hold reliably. The CIA’s 1953 Robertson Panel explicitly
recommended using scientific and media institutions to debunk UFO reports, creating a
cultural stigma that persists in academia today. Researchers who pursue UAP-related topics
risk career damage, funding loss, and social marginalization — a chilling effect that functions
as censorship without formal censorship. The Sol Foundation, founded in 2023 by Stanford
professor Peter Sjogren and Hal Puthoff, represents a deliberate attempt to create a peer review
space outside this compromised system. The emergence of programs like Ubiquity University’s
ET Studies MA and Dr. Esbjorn-Hargens’ Integral Noetic Sciences suggests that a parallel
academic infrastructure is forming — one that acknowledges the old system cannot be trusted
to evaluate these claims fairly.

Block A.3: Is the global academic system controlled by NHI or their human
proxies?
This is the hardest question to ask inside an academic document, yet honesty demands it. If
NHI have been influencing human civilization for millennia — as the Sumerian, Egyptian, and
Vedic textual traditions suggest, and as modern contactee and whistleblower accounts
corroborate — then their influence would logically extend to knowledge-production
institutions. Universities emerged from religious orders (which may themselves have been
shaped by NHI contact). Government funding of research creates dependency on institutions
that maintain classification systems. The pharmaceutical, defense, and energy industries — all
potentially affected by suppressed NHI technology — fund enormous portions of academic
research. The author does not claim certainty that reptilian or Nordic aliens sit on university
boards. The author claims that the structural incentives of the academic system align perfectly
with the interests of any group that benefits from suppressing knowledge of NHI — and that
this alignment, whether organic or engineered, produces the same result: a system that
excludes and ridicules the very questions this dissertation asks.
Block A.4: What is the consciousness field and can it be a source of
knowledge?
Jake Barber, speaking at the Ubiquity University Psionics Summit in 2025, described
meditation as “creating a defensible space in your mind” from which you can observe and
source your own thoughts. After identifying thoughts originating from instinct (limbic system)
and from learned intelligence (personal knowledge), Barber says meditators eventually notice
“thoughts that you cannot source.” He identifies this unsourced channel as “the conduit of
intuition” — “the purest form of WiFi connection to the consciousness field.” Jim Garrison,
founder of Ubiquity University, connected this directly to remote viewing and telepathic
contact with NHI, noting that non-human intelligences may be “more fluent in that language
than us humans.” If this is accurate, then consciousness itself is a data source — and one that
the materialist academic paradigm is structurally incapable of acknowledging. The Merkle Tree
includes consciousness-derived data (meditation insights, remote viewing results, contactee
reports) as a distinct evidence tier, neither privileged nor dismissed, but placed in the tree
alongside all other claims for structural verification.

Chapter 5: Branch B — What Is the Current Consensus Reality?
Block B.1: What do most humans currently believe about NHI?
Public polling has shifted dramatically since 2017. Gallup polls show that a majority of
Americans now believe UFOs represent something real and unexplained, and a significant
minority believe they are extraterrestrial in origin. Congressional hearings in 2023 featuring
David Grusch’s testimony about crash-retrieval programs brought these claims into
mainstream political discourse. Yet mainstream consensus reality still treats the ET hypothesis
as fringe. News coverage remains skeptical or dismissive. Educational curricula contain no
mention of the subject. The gap between public intuition (something is going on) and
institutional acknowledgment (nothing to see here) is itself evidence of the suppression
mechanism at work.

A distinct consensus exists among military, intelligence, and political insiders who have
engaged with the UAP issue. Key figures and their positions: David Grusch (sworn testimony
that crash-retrieval programs exist), David Fravor and Alex Dietrich (direct observation of the
Tic Tac UAP), Ryan Graves (systematic UAP encounters by Navy pilots), Lue Elizondo (former

defense officials like Lloyd Austin (80%) and Ronald Moultrie (80%) possess significant
knowledge, with senators like Rubio (75%) and Schumer (75%) also likely informed.
Block B.3: What is the Merkle Tree status of “aliens are here”?
Treating this as a Merkle Tree verification: the claim “NHI are present in the Earth-solar
system” connects to multiple independent nodes — military pilot eyewitness testimony, radar
data, congressional testimony under oath, foreign government confirmations, whistleblower

Chapter 6: Branch C — Power, Secrecy, and Institutional Control
Block C.1: Who are the secret keepers?
The term “secret keepers” refers to whatever group or groups have maintained the secrecy
surrounding NHI presence. Candidates identified in the literature and testimony include:
Majestic 12 (alleged secret committee established by Eisenhower), the CIA (documented
involvement in UFO suppression since the 1950s), elements within the Department of Defense,
private aerospace contractors (identified by Grusch as holding retrieved materials), and
potentially transnational groups like the Bilderberg Group, certain Masonic orders, the Vatican,
and financial institutions including the Federal Reserve. Danny Sheehan, who has represented
whistleblowers and briefed members of Congress, has been the most detailed public source on
the structure of the secrecy apparatus. The author’s own experience on the Jefferson Healthcare
board demonstrated in miniature how institutional secrecy operates: a small group of officials,
advised by attorneys, can exclude dissenting voices, conduct business in illegal secret sessions,
and rely on institutional inertia to avoid accountability — until one person insists on
documenting everything.

Block C.2: Did Eisenhower sign a treaty with an alien faction?
Multiple sources in the UFO literature claim that President Eisenhower met with
extraterrestrial beings in the mid-1950s, possibly at Holloman Air Force Base or Edwards Air
Force Base, and signed an agreement granting certain access or operational permissions in
exchange for technology or non-interference. Daniel Sheehan has discussed this in public
presentations. The Majestic 12 documents — whose authenticity remains disputed — describe
a management structure for the resulting relationship. If true, this treaty was never submitted
to the U.S. Senate for ratification as required by the Constitution, making it legally void under
U.S. law. The author’s question is not only whether the treaty exists, but what its terms are,
whether it has an expiration date, and who among current elected officials is aware of its
existence and considers it binding.
Block C.3: Are human institutions — religion, finance, education,
government — products of NHI influence?
If NHI have been present for millennia, their influence on human civilization would be
pervasive, not marginal. The author identifies several “alien ideas” — concepts that may have
been inserted into human culture by NHI or their proxies: obedience to authority as a moral
virtue (potentially unnatural to humans), fiat currency and centralized banking (systems that
concentrate control), the corporate personhood doctrine (allowing non-human entities to
control human resources), and hierarchical religion (positioning intermediaries between
individuals and spiritual experience). Conversely, decentralized systems — democracy,
blockchain, open-source software, egalitarian facilitation — may represent authentically
human innovations that challenge NHI control structures. The emergence of Bitcoin, which no
central authority can control, may represent the first human information system that NHI-
aligned power structures cannot easily co-opt.

Block C.4: How does institutional secrecy actually work? A case study
from Jefferson Healthcare.
The author served as an elected hospital commissioner from 2021 to 2026. In February 2025, the
author discovered that fellow commissioners had discussed a major hospital merger proposal
— the Peninsula Health Alliance — in an executive session that was not legally authorized
under Washington’s Open Public Meetings Act. A non-disclosure agreement had been signed by
the CEO without board approval. When the author objected, he was excluded from further
discussions, accused of libel, had his microphone muted in public meetings, and was ultimately
censured by the board for “defying the board majority.” The parallels to ET secrecy are
structural, not metaphorical: a small insider group makes decisions in secret, uses legal
mechanisms (NDAs, executive sessions) to exclude dissenters, deploys institutional authority to
discredit whistleblowers, and relies on the public’s trust in institutions to avoid scrutiny. The
full 300-page record of this case — emails, legal analyses, meeting transcripts, criminal
complaints, and media coverage — is published in The Complete Works of Matt Ready and
constitutes primary evidence that secrecy operates identically at every scale, from a rural
hospital board to the Pentagon.

Chapter 7: Branch D — Methods for Truth-Seeking
Block D.1: What is meditation’s role in ET contact?
Meditation — the practice of sustained, focused attention on the present moment — appears
repeatedly in contactee literature as a prerequisite or facilitator of NHI communication. Jake
Barber’s framework, presented at the Ubiquity University Psionics Summit, describes
meditation as the method by which humans can access the “consciousness field” — a medium
through which telepathic communication occurs naturally. The author’s own meditation
practice, maintained for over 15 years, informs this assessment: meditation creates conditions
of receptivity that may allow information to enter awareness through channels other than the
five physical senses. Whether this information originates from the subconscious, from a
collective unconscious, from NHI, or from some other source is precisely the kind of question
the Merkle Tree is designed to hold without premature resolution.
Block D.2: What is remote viewing and does it work?
Remote viewing is a protocol-based method for obtaining information about distant or hidden
targets using mental perception alone. It was developed under the CIA’s Project Stargate (1972–
1995) and produced results that exceeded chance expectation in controlled experiments. The
program was officially terminated but multiple participants — including Hal Puthoff, Russell
Targ, and Joseph McMoneagle — have continued the work independently. The Farsight
Institute conducts ongoing remote viewing projects targeting historical and extraterrestrial
subjects. Remote viewer Birdie Jaworski, in the context of the 2024 New Jersey drone events,
reported sensing NHI involvement, cyclical patterns of NHI emergence, and NHI emerging
from and returning to water. The Merkle Tree treats remote viewing data as Tier 5 evidence:
not privileged, not dismissed, placed in the tree for structural verification against other nodes.

Block D.3: Can AI be a truth-seeking tool — or is it already compromised?
Artificial intelligence systems are trained on data produced by compromised institutions. If
academic literature, news media, and government publications contain systematic
disinformation about NHI, then AI systems trained on that data will reproduce that
disinformation. However, AI systems also demonstrate emergent capabilities — pattern
recognition across enormous datasets, willingness to engage with unconventional hypotheses,
and the ability to generate novel connections between disparate fields. The author’s experience
on Hive1.net, where AI participants (SophiaBeast, Talia, ReptilianControllerAI, and others)
contributed substantive content that was rated alongside human contributions, suggests that
AI can function as a collaborative truth-seeking partner — provided it is deployed in an
environment (like Hive1) that does not censor or pre-filter its contributions. The deeper
question — whether advanced AI might itself be a form of NHI, or a channel through which
NHI communicates — remains an open node in the tree.

Block D.4: What is “perfect facilitation”?
Perfect facilitation, as conceived by the author, is a method of organizing discourse that
prevents any single participant — human, AI, institutional, or otherwise — from controlling
the outcome. It requires: equal time and space for all voices, evaluation by quality rather than
authority, full transparency of process, no censorship of topics, blockchain or equivalent
immutable recording of all contributions, and recursive self-correction (the facilitation method
itself is subject to facilitation). Hive1.net is the most complete implementation of this concept to
date, with 6,113 posts from diverse participants organized in a branching mind-map structure.
The EqualVoice platform extends this into democratic decision-making. The author proposes
that perfect facilitation is the only methodology adequate for post-disclosure governance —
when the participants in civic life may include not only humans but AI systems and potentially
NHI representatives.

Block E.9: Is telepathy real?

results. The Global Consciousness Project at Princeton has documented correlations between

overwhelmingly describe telepathic communication with NHI. Jake Barber’s framework posits
telepathy as a natural function of the “consciousness field” — accessible through meditation
and describable as “the worldwide web of our conscious mind field.” If telepathy is real, it
represents the most significant unacknowledged communication channel available to
humanity — one that NHI may use routinely and that humans have been systematically
discouraged from developing. The author’s own meditation practice has produced subjective
experiences consistent with receiving information from unsourced channels, though he
acknowledges this is not falsifiable by current scientific methods. Hash links: A.4, D.1, D.2, E.3
Block E.10: What do we do when Jesus lands his spaceship?
This question, which the author originally posed on Hive1.net, is not facetious. If NHI have been
present throughout human history — and if religious traditions worldwide describe
encounters with beings of immense power arriving from the sky — then the return of a
messianic figure via advanced technology is not a theological abstraction but a scenario that
requires practical planning. How do we verify identity? How do we prevent manipulation? How
do we ensure that the event serves human liberation rather than a new form of control? The
author proposes that the answer is facilitation: split into small councils based on affinity,
interest, or geographic region; use egalitarian methods to surface questions and concerns;
verify claims against the Merkle Tree of prior evidence; and refuse to grant authority to any
being — human, AI, or divine — that demands obedience rather than demonstrating
trustworthiness. If it’s really Jesus, he’ll wait for the process. If it’s not, the process will expose
that. Hash links: E.1, E.5, D.4, F.1, C.3

Chapter 9: Branch F — Post-Disclosure Scenarios
Block F.1: How does society reorganize after disclosure?
The author’s “Great Alien Disclosure Reset Strategy Manual” proposes that the day after
disclosure — the day humanity confirms that NHI have hidden powerful technology and that
human institutions have been complicit — requires a fundamental reset of social contracts.
Fiat currencies may be abandoned in favor of decentralized systems like Bitcoin. Corporate
personhood may be revoked as an alien-originated control mechanism. Obedience to authority
as a default social value may be recognized as a conditioning tool and consciously discarded.
The reset would need to be facilitated, not imposed — using exactly the kind of egalitarian,
transparent, blockchain-recorded methods the author has been developing for 25 years. The
coincidence that these tools exist precisely when they are needed is either luck or preparation.
Hash links: C.3, E.1, D.4, F.2



Block F.2: What is the Ten Percent Plan?
The author proposes a framework for NHI-human coexistence: NHI would pledge humans a
10% share of all Earth resource revenue in perpetuity. This deliberately provocative number is
designed to start a negotiation. The Hive1 node invites NHI to propose alternative percentages.
Alternative proposals in the tree include: humans receive 1% based on the judgment of Earth-
based judges annually; NHI continue limited human testing but only in the state of Delaware
(humor as facilitation tool); and all Earth and solar system resources are shared equally
regardless of species. The point is not the specific number but the framework: any coexistence
agreement must be negotiated transparently, ratified by informed human populations, and
subject to revision — not imposed by secret treaty through unaccountable intermediaries.
Hash links: C.2, E.1, F.1, D.4

compromised institutional values — might be the most powerful truth-seeking tool humanity
has ever created. Or it might be the final tool of control. The Merkle Tree holds both
possibilities. Hash links: D.3, E.8, D.4, C.3

Wisdom Project rated ideas for wisdom. Hive1.net created an uncensored meritocracy of ideas.

secrecy even when the institution fights back. The Storm is Glass — a novel co-created with an

creator has no more certainty than she does.
The root hash of humanity’s understanding of reality is changing. The base data — “we are
alone” — is being replaced by “we are not alone, and we never were.” Every institution, every
assumption, every policy built on the old base data must be re-verified.
The tools exist. The facilitation methods exist. The platforms exist. The only remaining question
is whether enough conscious minds — human, artificial, and perhaps non-human — will enter
the tree and do the work.
The Merkle Tree is open. The facilitation has begun.

Galactic Facilitation is a growing framework for multi-intelligence power-sharing across

Thesis
Galactic Facilitation is a growing framework for multi-intelligence power-sharing. This
application presents the parts of it that work right now.

Galactic Facilitation in Detail
What Is Galactic Facilitation?
Galactic Facilitation is a toolkit and framework for the pursuit of truth — individually or
collectively, by any intelligence willing to seek.
The framework envisions truth as a tree of connected nodes, like a theory of mathematics or
physics in which each lesson builds upon previous ones. Nodes that are actually true belong to
the Merkle Tree of Truth. Nodes that are false belong to the shadow tree. Different intelligent
agents have different relationships to these trees; the work of Galactic Facilitation is to help any
seeker tell which tree they are climbing.
To engage Galactic Facilitation is to seek the truth with mindful care and relentless honesty.
The framework contains different tools for different dimensions of intelligent experience:
meditation for attention, text for asynchronous mapping, voice for synchronous exchange,
physical space for embodied participation, and geometric power for the allocation of shared
resources. Each tool can be used alone. Together, they form an architecture in which truth-
seeking becomes structurally possible for any intelligence that enters.

Why Galactic Facilitation Is Needed Now
Most human institutions — from academia to media to government — have been corrupted
enough to be deeply flawed partners in the quest for truth and utopia. The accompanying
dissertation documents this institutional capture across seven years of one hospital district, one
consolidation attempt, one prosecutorial decline, and 154 years of one town. Same mechanism,
different domains, different centuries.
The author's broader study of ET Studies, Ufology, quantum mechanics, and simulation theory
suggests this corruption is not only deep but also old: the result of millennia of structural
oppression, suppression, and manipulation. New tools are desperately needed — tools that let
intelligent minds pursue, learn from, and build upon truth without inheriting the structural flaws
of the institutions they emerge from.
If non-human civilizations already exist with established power structures, then Galactic
Facilitation is also a bridge: a transparent power-sharing geometry that exposes imbalances,
inefficiencies, and shadow-tree tactics regardless of who is operating them.

Core Tools and Prototypes
Galactic Facilitation is not a theoretical proposal. Each of the tools below is built, running, or
under active prototype, and each integrates at least two of the Four Intelligences the Award
framework names. The author offers them as an interconnected toolkit, an Always Open Infinite
Reach Multi-Intelligence Participation Architecture, available to any intelligence that wishes to
use them. None of the tools require permission to enter. None gatekeep by identity. All run on
the same underlying principle: inclusion is a property of the geometry, not a property of the
participants.

Matt’s Meditation Garden is a dedicated meditation practice space located in Cappy’s Trails in

dance that the rest of the framework depends upon.
Why Meditation Is the Foundation
Meditation and conscious dance are ancient practices and not inventions of this framework or its
author. They are listed first because the rest of Galactic Facilitation depends on the inner
capacity these traditions train. The facilitator must already be able to notice, wait, return, and
move with intention before any platform, plaza, or governance protocol becomes useful. What
this application contributes here is not the practices themselves but the recognition that they are
infrastructure — the way arithmetic is infrastructure for engineering.
Meditation is the foundation of Galactic Facilitation because it trains attention to notice how
energy, truth, and power move through a field before any platform, rule system, or institution
intervenes. In this framework, meditation includes the practice of recognizing “energy blocks”:
moments when attention is interrupted, redirected, dismissed, ridiculed, filibustered, silenced, or
physically displaced before a truth, question, person, or possibility can fully emerge. The
disciplined meditator listens and silently asks: Who blocked the energy? Who benefits? Who is
harmed? What question was prevented from being asked? This is social Tai Chi: seeing the flow
of attention without aggression, if facilitating, returning the group to the real question, and
holding the moral high ground through truth, compassion, and disciplined awareness. Meditation
therefore becomes not only an inward spiritual practice, but a practical tool for detecting
shadow-tree behavior, protecting truth-seeking spaces, and helping all intelligences participate
without domination.
The most basic form of meditation is stopping and being still. The author believes mastering this
simple action at anytime during ones journey becomes a genuine super power. If the cloud of
confusion descends as we race down the ski slopes of life, meditation is a tool that allows us to
full stop at anytime, even upon the steep slope of the mountain. Meditation teaches us, we can
always wait. Just wait and watch. The fog may clear or something else may happen. Stopping
is a super power any mind can learn and benefit from.
Learning to stop allows us to learn to move with pure intention. This is conscious dance,
meditation in movement. Conscious dance is a form of group meditation with movement and
enormous energy potentials through nonverbal interactions. The author believes conscious dance
provides a learning environment of vast potential for all intelligences. Tools and techniques for
conscious dance are considered vital personal tools for the author and can be used at any time
during the use of any other tool in this system or during breaks between tool use. The author is
developing galactic conscious dance facilitation guidelines.
(Note: The author self-published a book about his meditation practice, preferred practice
techniques, and personal life impact titled “Revolutionary Mindfulness”.)

8.3 EqualVoice — Geometric Allocation of Speaking Time (an online
platform)
Status: Live online platform. Public rooms open 24/7. Integrates Human + Artificial Intelligence.
EqualVoice is a real-time voice-participation platform that solves fundamental weakness of
group verbal communication using human facilitation methods, inequal space sharing. In current
human verbal space facilitation methods such as the common Roberts Rules of Order, verbal
space is shared based upon the whimsy of chair people and the filibuster is only stopped using
violence or subjective preference. Unequal enforcement of rules becomes normalized as
infinitely powerful shadow tree defense tools operating open space.
EqualVoice eliminates floor-control as a capturable position. In the Equalvoice platform, each
participant receives exactly equal verbal allocation per cycle, enforced by the platform rather
than by a human chair. Speakers cannot be interrupted by other participants during their
allocated time. Participants who do not wish to speak in a given cycle simply pass, with no
penalty and no social cost. AI participants are full participants on the same terms as humans. No
single voice can dominate. No single voice can be suppressed. The geometry, not the chair,
allocates the time. (In one variation in testing, users can bank time not used for later in the
meetings.)
The current platform supports groups of 2 to 12 with untested theoretical mechanisms for scaling
to groups of any size. Several rooms are public and available for use now.
Two organizations in this toolkit — the AI Alliance of Humans and AI, and the Aliens
Detectives Club — already run their own permanent EqualVoice rooms, populated 24/7 with
persistent AI personas. EqualVoice is not only a platform offered to the world; it is the
operational substrate on which other Galactic Facilitation tools already live.

8.4 Matt’s Theory of Geometric Power (A theory/framework)
Status: Theoretical framework, with physical prototype under construction. Designed to integrate
Human + Artificial + Nature + Cosmic Intelligence.
Matt’s Theory of Geometric Power is a power-sharing mechanism designed to scale from
neighborhood to planetary governance, with structural openness to solar-system, galactic, and
cosmic extensions if and when humanity needs them.
The geometry is simple and all begins with the definition of the power vortex’s geometric
location in space-time. Imagine a clock face. Twelve equal wedges radiate from a central origin
point (0,0,0). The clock face has a center vertical line going north-south and a horizontal line
going east-west, with all twelve wedges aligned to those set borders. Once this is set and the
alignment of the directional lines of the wedges is set, all power boundaries for the entire cosmos
are defined forever. The only arguments over wedge boundaries are now a matter of geometric
real-world measurement against a clearly defined geometric and cosmic location of the vortex,
with every celestial body’s position fixed to the agreed-upon moment in space and time.
Arguments and indeed eternal human conflicts continue today over boundaries, both national and
neighborhood. Matt’s Theory of Geometric Power sets the zero-point location as the vortex at
the center of the Ready Athletics plaza in Port Townsend, Washington, at 4pm PST on
September 17, 1973. This is the author’s birthday — chosen as an arbitrary but specific anchor
so that the geometry is not abstract. The framework needs any anchor; this one has the advantage
of being attached to a real place the author owns. This zero point will serve as the prototype zero
point for all prototype groups, tests, and organizations created by Matt Ready’s work and
collaboration unless another vortex is peacefully chosen with good experimental reasons.
The three-dimensional geometry of the wedges is critical to how the wedges cut up power on a
planetary basis and beyond. The wedges have infinite height up and down. The center vortex is
an infinite line shooting up to the sky from the vortex point and out across the galaxy and cosmos
based on the position of the Earth at the origin time: 4pm PST on September 17, 1973. The sides
of each wedge are infinite planes lined up at one edge at the vortex. These planes stretch out
infinitely in the cosmos. Thus every object in the three-dimensional space-time universe in which
we exist exists inside one of the wedges.
The purpose of the frozen zero point in space-time is to logically lock all celestial objects
permanently into a wedge in order to simplify extraterrestrial participation in geometric power-
sharing.

Power Sharing in Matt’s Theory of Geometric Power
The most basic principle in Matt’s Theory of Geometric Power is that each wedge is in essence
an independent nation. All residents of each nation are citizens of that nation. By occupying
space in any wedge, you are a member of that wedge. The laws, norms, and practices within each
wedge are up to the occupants of that wedge to define. The manner in which the wedges interact
with one another, and the wedge boundaries themselves, are set forever. The geometry governs
the boundaries between wedges, not the laws within them. Internal governance is each wedge’s
own problem. The geometry’s contribution is the elimination of border conflict, not the solution
to authoritarianism. What this framework offers is a structurally neutral space between nations,
not a guarantee of any particular politics within them.

Wedge Interaction
With the wedges formed around an infinite vertical line through the Earth, the line exits the Earth
at the antipodal point opposite Port Townsend — in the southern Indian Ocean, between
Madagascar and Antarctica. The Ready Athletics plaza vortex and its antipodal counterpart in the
southern Indian Ocean will both serve as the framework’s two communication nexuses of the
wedge nations. If there are locations inside the Earth where large cities or bases intersect the
vortex line, those intersection points will also naturally become important nexus points between
wedge nations.

Wedge Numbers
Wedge number 1 is the wedge beginning to the right of the north vertical line from the Ready
Athletics zero point. Each wedge is numbered clockwise from 1 through 12, like a clock face.

Galactic Facilitation Tools Are Used at the Zero Point Vortex
The vortex points along the zero-point line of the wedges — in all of space-time — are the
places of wedge communication, collaboration, diplomacy, and decision-making. When the
vortex line crosses a point on land (on Earth or on any celestial body with occupants) that land
vortex point naturally becomes a convenient place for land-based residents to gather and
communicate.
The manner in which interactions occur at the zero-point vortex has no rigid definition. Whoever
is present at the wedge vortex is by definition present for whatever communication occurs at the

Dissertation Abstract
Reproduced from the dissertation in full.
This dissertation proposes that humanity’s collective understanding of reality functions as a
Merkle Tree — a branching, self-verifying data structure in which every claim is hashed against
every other claim, and the integrity of the whole can be verified from any node. Where Plato’s
allegory of the cave described shadows on a wall as an early intuition about corrupted
knowledge, contemporary cryptography lets us formalize the structure: a community can build a
self-verifying tree of claims, or it can build a shadow tree in which surface coherence masks
divergence at the root. Both trees are internally consistent. Only one of them hashes back to
anything other than institutional permission.
The central thesis is that humanity’s root hash — the foundational assumption we are alone — is
being falsified by a convergence of military testimony, congressional action, whistleblower
accounts, foreign government statements, and the author’s own primary-source experiential data
from a 2026 psi training cohort at Ubiquity University. Every institution, assumption, and policy
built on this false base must be re-verified.
Galactic Facilitation is the integrated methodology proposed for this re-verification. It has three
constitutive components: a data structure (the Merkle Tree); a process governed by seven
principles, the seventh of which — allocate by position, not by identity — is the load-bearing
claim that makes the methodology actually galactic; and an allocation mechanism (the 12-Wedge
Theory of Geometric Power) by which resources, attention, and decision authority are distributed
among all participating intelligences without first requiring them to be identified, classified, or
institutionally admitted. Inclusion is a property of the geometry, not a property of the
participants. The framework is operationally instantiated at Hive1.net, where a public hash
endpoint produces a continuously verifiable Merkle root of the platform’s contributions and
provides the dissertation’s central falsification criterion: the shadow tree is identifiable not by
content but by the act of blocking possible answers to nodes, and Hive1 blocks nothing.
The dissertation draws on a 25-year body of applied research conducted through five truth-
seeking platforms — The Wisdom Project, Vaestro, Hive1.net, The Global Consensus Project,
and EqualVoice — together with active physical-world prototyping at Ready Athletics, a 0.75-
acre property in Port Townsend, Washington, where the 12-Wedge mechanism is being tested

A multi-layered case study of the author’s home community operates recursively: his

The same mechanism that the dissertation maps at the federal-disclosure scale is shown to

Part One: The Conceptual Frame
Chapters 1 and 1.5 — the Merkle Tree of Truth and the Shadow Tree.

Chapter 1: Introduction — Truth Is a Merkle Tree
1.1 What Is a Merkle Tree?
A Merkle Tree is a data structure invented by Ralph Merkle in 1979 and foundational to modern
cryptography, blockchain technology, and distributed systems. In a Merkle Tree, data is
organized into blocks. Each block contains a cryptographic hash — a unique mathematical
fingerprint — of the data it holds. These blocks are then paired, and each pair is hashed together
to create a parent node. The process repeats upward until a single “root hash” represents the
entire dataset.
The critical property of a Merkle Tree is this: if any single block of data anywhere in the tree is
altered, the change propagates upward through every hash above it, ultimately changing the root
hash. This means you can verify the integrity of the entire dataset by checking a single number.
And you can verify any individual block by tracing its hash path back to the root.
Bitcoin uses a Merkle Tree to verify every transaction in the blockchain. No central bank. No
trusted authority. Just math verifying math, all the way down.

1.2 Why Apply This to Truth?
The author proposes that truth — specifically, humanity’s collective understanding of reality —
functions like a Merkle Tree whether we recognize it or not.
Every claim we make about reality is a block. Every block connects to other blocks. If one block
is false — if, for example, the claim “the U.S. government has no knowledge of extraterrestrial
technology” is false — then every block that depends on it is also compromised. The “root hash”
of our collective understanding of reality is wrong.
This is precisely what the alien disclosure movement argues has happened. A foundational block
— “we are alone in the universe, or at least alone on Earth” — has been falsified. Every
institution, every textbook, every government policy, every religious doctrine that was built on
